Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?

Status: answer

Answer:

In GregTech: New Horizons, overclocking a machine recipe reduces its duration and increases its EU/t. A regular overclock multiplies EU/t by 4 and divides duration by 2, so total energy (EU/t × duration) doubles. A perfect overclock also multiplies EU/t by 4 and divides duration by 2, but it additionally reduces the total energy cost by a factor of 2 compared to the original recipe, so total energy stays the same as the un-overclocked recipe. In short: regular overclock = 4× EU/t, 1/2 duration, 2× total EU; perfect overclock = 4× EU/t, 1/2 duration, 1× total EU.

Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?

Status: answer

Answer:

Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and double the total EU consumption, which quadruples EU/t usage (hence "2/4 overclocking"). Perfect overclocks instead quadruple the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same, which also quadruples EU/t usage (hence "4/4 overclocking").

For this reason, perfect overclocking is also called 4/4 overclocking.\nMachines typically receive one overclock per voltage tier above the minimum required for a recipe.\nSingleblock machines can only ever regular overclock.\nMultiblock machines perfect overclock on a case-by-case basis; their tooltips contain information on how to achieve perfect overclocks or upgrade overclocks to perfect overclocks. If no information is mentioned, they will regular overclock.\nMultiblocks with two energy hatches of the same voltage will always draw 4A to overclock a recipe to a tier higher than the energy hatch voltage (since 4A of the lower voltage contains the same EU as 1A of the higher voltage). This also allows them to run recipes with a minimum requirement of that higher voltage tier.\nCables and Loss\nGregTech EU can be transferred using GregTech Cables.\nRather than priority by destination, power priority is given by cardinal direction. Cables will push power in the following priority:\n- Down\n- Up\n- North\n- South\n- West\n- East\nWhen producing power, each generator will always attempt to empty all of its internal buffer at once. This can cause one generator in a cable network"

A power outputting singleblock will take 8 × 4 t i e r + 2 m a x ( 0 , t i e r − 1 ) {\\displaystyle {\\displaystyle 8\\times 4^{tier}+2^{max(0,tier-1)}}} EU from its internal buffer and output 8 × 4 t i e r {\\displaystyle {\\displaystyle 8\\times 4^{tier}}} EU (which is always the maximum EU one amp of that voltage tier can hold). In Step Up mode, they draw up to 4 amps of a lower voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers"
- candidate `chunk-25298a8ccfa52b75ddf2ff553426966f` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=0-400 distance=0.333651 similarity=0.666349 sections=[Electricity Electricity > Voltage and Amperage Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Quick Tip Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. EU is used to run GregTech and IC2 machines. Every Tier offers multiple types of Power Generation options at LV and above. EU is also compatible with machines from Applied Energistics 2 and other machines that accept Redstone Flux (RF), converting at a rate of 1 EU to 3.6 RF. The reverse is not possible; RF cannot be converted to EU.\nVoltage and Amperage\nAcronym | Voltage Tier | EU Limit\nAcronym: ULV | Voltage Tier: Ultra Low Voltage | EU Limit: 8\nAcronym: LV | Voltage Tier: Low Voltage | EU Limit: 32\nAcronym: MV | Voltage Tier: Medium Voltage | EU Limit: 128\nAcronym: HV | Voltage Tier: High Voltage | EU Limit: 512\nAcronym: EV | Voltage Tier: Extreme Voltage | EU Limit: 2,048\nAcronym: IV | Voltage Tier: Insane Voltage | EU Limit: 8,192\nAcronym: LuV | Voltage Tier: Ludicrous Voltage | EU Limit: 32,768\nAcronym: ZPM | Voltage Tier: ZPM Voltage | EU Limit: 131,072\nAcronym: UV | Voltage Tier: Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 524,288\nAcronym: UHV | Voltage Tier: Highly Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 2,097,152\nAcronym: UEV | Voltage Tier: Extremely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 8,388,608\nAcronym: UIV | Voltage Tier: Insanely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 33,554,432\nAcronym: UMV | Voltage Tier: Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 134,217,728\nAcronym: UXV | Voltage Tier: Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 536,870,912\nAcronym: MAX | Voltage Tier: Maximum Voltage | EU Limit: 2,147,483,648\nEU in GregTech comes in a system of Voltage (Volts, V) and Amperage (Amps, A).\nEnergy is transferred in packages. Voltage describes the size of the energy packages, while Amperage describes the number of packages. When you multiply both, you get the power in EU/t (Energy Units per tick), which describes the energy produced, transferred, or consumed over time.\nQuick Tip\n- If you have X generators of Tier Y, use cables that can handle X Amperes of Tier Y.\nVoltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage"
- candidate `chunk-fb8a11eb2b47d2c1a0f004bd9cb9e207` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=320-720 distance=0.335919 similarity=0.664081 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Quick Tip Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Amperage] text="of Tier Y, use cables that can handle X Amperes of Tier Y.\nVoltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on.\nAmperage\nIn code, amps are pushed, not pulled. However, they are only pushed when requested by machines. Thus, for all scopes except pack development, you can assume amps are only ever pulled as needed.\nMachines and energy hatches draw amps to fill their internal EU buffers. The capacity of the internal buffer is listed as \"Capacity:\" in the machine's or hatch's tooltip. When processing a recipe, a machine will draw from its internal buffer. The current contents of the internal buffer can be checked with the Portable Scanner .\nThe maximum amount of amps a machine can draw is either listed on its tooltip or recipe-dependent. A machine can draw up to a maximum of ⌊ 2 × Recipe Usage EU/t Voltage Tier EU Limit ⌋ + 1 {\\displaystyle {\\displaystyle \\left\\lfloor {\\frac {2\\times {\\text{Recipe Usage EU/t}}}{\\text{Voltage Tier EU Limit}}}\\right\\rfloor +1}} amps to fill its internal buffer. This means that if the machine isn't processing a recipe, it will draw 1 amp to refill the internal buffer. Recipe amperages listed in NEI are a recommended number to fill the internal buffer at a rate that breaks even against usage.\nSeveral common amperages of GregTech machines can be found in the table below. \"Drawing\" means \"draws up to\", unless otherwise stated.\nOutput amps contain the maximum EU for the outputting machine's voltage tier.\nMachine | Notes\nMachine: Singleblock Generators | Notes: Output 1A of its tier\nMachine: Energy Hatches | Notes: Draws 2A (second amp mostly for extra draw for loss)\nMachine: Step-up Transformers | Notes: Draws 4A lower voltage, outputs 1A higher voltage\nMachine: Step-down Transformers | Notes:"
- candidate `chunk-16d1ae576cd649fa3c6fee16783cff7a` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=960-1360 distance=0.345178 similarity=0.654822 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > GT Electric Machines Low Voltage (LV) > Explosions Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Conversion Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Conversion > IC2 EU Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Conversion > GT EU to Others] text="stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.\nSome machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . The Arc Furnace requires 3 amps to function and can accept up to 7 amps. Checking any recipe for the Arc Furnace will show Usage XX/t, voltage 32 EU/t and amperage X. The Electric Blast Furnace is even more demanding, taking four amps of LV minimum for its most basic recipes.\nExplosions\nMachines, wires and cables can overload, resulting in fires and explosions .\nRain will make your electric machines explode if the rain is on any adjacent blocks to the machine, so put your machinery under a proper roof. Uninsulated wires will also catch on fire from rain. Fire adjacent to machines will cause them to explode, potentially taking out more machines and causing significant Pollution . Water does not cause fires/explosions; it's perfectly safe to have water blocks adjacent to machines.\nGiving machines a higher voltage than they are rated for will make them explode. This won't become an issue before unlocking MV , but it's important enough to mention early and often. Excess Amperage on a cable is not an issue, as long as it doesn't exceed the cable's rating. Machines will only accept as many Amps as they need.\nEnergy Conversion\nIC2 EU\nTo transform IC2 energy into GT energy you simply need to place a GT transformer or power storage next to the IC2 power source. Keep in mind that IC2 generation is typically only 1 amp, therefore the Transformer should be in Step-Down mode. GT cables/wires can be used to connect IC2 machines, but pay attention to the EU output. Some devices such as the Stirling Generator output more than 32EU, and thus require at least x2 cable.\nGT EU to Others\nGT Cables can be attached to almost any machine that requires some kind of energy, allowing a single power network to run machines from most mods in the pack including IC2, EnderIO, Forestry, Railcraft, Galacticraft and more. Due to the idiosyncrasies of ENet, at least one GT machine (a machine hull will do the job nicely) has to be present for power to transfer on GT cables/wires. Placing"
- candidate `chunk-65604eae038cd0f996e8385eb1f9214b` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=1280-1680 distance=0.350220 similarity=0.649780 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > UHV Capacitor Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Electric Implosion Compressor Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Component Assembly Line Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Integrated Ore Factory Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Compact Fusion Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Fusion Reactor Mk4] text="upgrade to power storage, providing effectively unlimited EU capacity and removing issues with the EU buffer size being too small to last through large crafts. This does mean that power production is likely to run 24/7, so players need to ensure their power and resource production can handle this. It also unlocks wireless EU between LSCs, but this is not advisable in UHV: any LSC with a UHV capacitor on wireless mode can only safely sustain 10B EU/t of output, significantly less than many multiblocks are likely to consume.\nElectric Implosion Compressor\nA Tier 1 Electric Implosion Compressor\nThe Electric Implosion Compressor works similar to the Implosion Compressor , but uses a small amount of energy instead of TNT, in addition to having faster recipes and support for TecTech energy hatches. While not strictly required, this should be built before the Tier 8 rocket.\nComponent Assembly Line\nA UV Tier Component Assembly Line\nThe UHV Component Assembly Line (CoAL) is very useful due to how often UHV components are used, particularly for UHV superconductors in Bio Mainframes, Compact Fusion Reactor Mk4s, and new multiblocks like the Integrated Ore Factory. Its extremely high Cosmic Neutronium cost makes it very difficult to afford prior to the Mk2 Space Elevator Mining Module, although sufficient investment into Meteors can also be used. Players who have not made any Component Assembly Line yet should make one in UHV.\nIntegrated Ore Factory\nThe Integrated Ore Factory is a large-scale ore processing multiblock that is unlocked with UEV circuits. It is able to process thousands of ores per second, and can do every step of ore processing in one machine, making it much faster, more scalable, and more performant than previous ore processing setups. Even with these benefits, it can often struggle to keep up with high-tier Space Elevator mining modules, requiring parallelization, overclocking with 2, 8, or even 32 energy hatches, or both. The IOF should be the only ore processor in lategame bases.\nCompact Fusion\nCompact Fusion Reactors (Compacts) are advanced versions of Fusion Reactors that condense 64 regular Fusion Reactors worth of throughput into a single multiblock with the cost of 48 Fusion Reactors of their tier. Although Compacts are available as early as LuV, UHV is where regular Fusion Reactors become largely obsolete due to how much the demand for fusion products increases.\nFusion Reactor Mk4\nThe Mk4 Fusion Reactor is available in"
- candidate `chunk-b5eae9882a140807ecb1a43eabe50f3e` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=4160-4560 distance=0.353344 similarity=0.646656 sections=[Electricity > Output Loss Electricity > Transformers Electricity > Transformers > Power Transformer and Hi-Amp Transformer Electricity > Transformers > Active Transformer Electricity > Trivia] text="64 | Loss (%): 0.048804 | Internal Buffer Consumption (EU): 131136\nTier: UV | Output (EU): 524288 | Loss (EU): 128 | Loss (%): 0.024408 | Internal Buffer Consumption (EU): 524416\nTransformers\nPicture of a Transformer in default mode transferring 1 amp of HV into 4 amps of MV.\nTransformers convert EU between voltage tiers. In Step Up mode, they draw up to 4 amps of a lower voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce 1A of a higher voltage. This can allow lower tier amps to power higher tier machines which may only draw 1-2 A for a recipe. Similarly, in Step Down mode, they draw 1 amp of a higher voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce up to 4A of a lower voltage. This allows use of higher tier power generators with lower tier machines while preventing explosions. Use a Soft Mallet to switch the mode.\nThe big dot with a plus is the high voltage side and is the front face, while the five smaller circles are the lower voltage sides. Regardless of mode, the big dot is always for the higher voltage. That means in Step Up mode, transformers have one output, five inputs, and in Step Down mode, they have five outputs, one input.\nThe output loss section above applies to transformer outputs as well.\nPower Transformer and Hi-Amp Transformer\nThe Power Transformer and the Hi-Amp Transformer work like an ordinary transformer with one exception:\nThe Hi-Amp Transformer will accept 4 amps of higher voltage and turn it into 16 amps of lower voltage in its default mode. In inverted mode it will transform 16amps lower voltage to 4 amps of higher voltage.\nThe Power Transformer will accept 16 amps of higher voltage and turn it into 64 amps of lower voltage in its default mode. In inverted mode it will transform 64 amps lower voltage to 16 amps of higher voltage.\nActive Transformer\nThe Active Transformer is a multiblock unlocked in ZPM tier that can transform to and from any voltage, accepting energy with an Energy Hatch and outputting energy with a Dynamo Hatch.\n- Note: Prior to Version 2.7.0 Wrenching or modifying the Active Transformer while it is running would cause it to explode.\nTrivia\n- GregTech's current power system is called the GT Enet API (Enet).\n-"
- candidate `chunk-7668692c22d0a7126a5d97c525457bc2` doc=doc-a509849f031bb1dadb346a8565bf75e8 words=1600-2000 distance=0.353544 similarity=0.646456 sections=[Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Power > Power Eye of Harmony Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Power > Wireless Energy Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Dimensional Convergence Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Machine Scaling] text="long as it does not run any overclocks or parallels. Power-generating EoHs can produce a maximum of 12.87T EU/t when running the T10 Deep Dark recipe with 9/9/9 casings, meaning that reaching the Stargate typically requires at least a hundred of them.\nWireless Energy\nUMV adds many new hatches for working with wireless energy, capable of replacing non-wireless energy for everything except multiblocks that need laser hatches. UXV circuits unlock UIV and UMV Wireless Energy Hatches, meaning that unlike in UIV, it is possible to use wireless for on-tier power. In addition, Shirabon unlocks multi-amp (although not laser) Wireless Energy Hatches, which are helpful for multiblocks like the Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver or Quantum Computer , that accept multi-amp hatches and either don't accept or don't need laser hatches. The UMV Capacitor can also be used to download up to 10P EU/t to a Lapotronic Supercapacitor , for any multiblocks that need enough energy from laser hatches that the UIV Capacitor is insufficient.\nUMV also introduces the only wireless Dynamo Hatch, the Energized Wireless Dynamo Hatch, which can be used on Dyson Swarm Ground Units or Large Naquadah Reactors (although not the Stabilized Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix ) and can output up to 65,536 amps of UMV (approximately 8.8T EU/t) directly to the wireless network. Crafting it requires an Eye of Harmony, as the recipe uses Stellar Catalyst.\nDimensional Convergence\nSee More: DTPF#Dimensional Convergence\nDimensional Convergence is a mechanic that can be used to gain perfect overclocks for the DTPF , at the cost of increased catalyst consumption. It is unlocked in UMV, requiring UMV Energy Hatches and Field Generators to make the Transdimensional Alignment Matrix that is used to activate it in a DTPF. Although convergence is never required, it is very useful for avoiding DTPF spam or immense power consumption in the endgame. However, because it requires a full catalyst discount to run, using convergence demands the ability to run a DTPF passively with 100% uptime, including the increased speed and catalyst usage of convergence. An Eye of Harmony running the Deep Dark recipe can help with this, as that recipe produces all 16 plasmas used for Exotic Catalyst.\nMachine Scaling\nBuilding the Eye of Harmony requires robust on-demand crafting infrastructure, especially for its higher tier casings. In order to bring the crafting time for Eye of Harmony parts to a reasonable level, UMV demands players to scale their arrays"
- candidate `chunk-98c3ec36605b3ea411d9d86f356773f2` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=1280-1680 distance=0.358182 similarity=0.641818 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Infrastructure > Circuits Insane Voltage (IV) > Infrastructure > Smelting] text="as the Assembly Line that gates LuV.\nIn addition to the new circuit line, lower tier circuits also get upgrades. Multiblocks like the Industrial Wire Factory , Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver , and Precise Assembler greatly speed the process of making circuit components. Naquadah, which can be found either rarely in End asteroids or on the Asteroids dimension with a tier 3 rocket, can be processed slowly in the EBF to yield Naquadah Nuggets, which can be used to make the next tier of silicon boule and thereby unlock better wafer recipes. One of these recipes is SoC Wafers, which are used in better LV and MV circuit recipes. Advanced SMDs, although requiring advanced materials such as PBI and platline metals, can also be used to replace regular SMDs in earlier circuit recipes, allowing them to be crafted twice as fast and with a quarter of the SMD requirements.\nBecause of the very high circuit demands of late IV and LuV, it is highly recommended to parallelize circuit crafting by using multiple Circuit Assemblers, as the multiblock Circuit Assembly Line is unavailable until LuV.\nSmelting\nIV is a tier that demands a lot of capacity to smelt ingots in the Electric Blast Furnace and cool them in the Vacuum Freezer , but it is also a tier that unlocks major upgrades to meet this demand. HSS-G Coils are available as soon as the Assembling Machine is crafted, and should be a priority upgrade for the energy discounts, new recipes, and perfect overclocks they can reach. HSS-S Coils are not required, but are unlocked upon completing the platline, and are very valuable for the same reasons. IV is also a good time to look at upgrading beyond helium for those EBF recipes that require a noble gas; these gases can be made with liquid Overworld/Nether Air processing, bees, or the Radon loop. The more interesting upgrades, however, revolve around using better versions of the EBF and VF that allow greater throughput.\nVolcanus\nOne of these upgrades is the Volcanus , a superior version of the EBF which is over twice as fast, supports up to 8 parallels, and has a 10% energy discount. However, it requires 10 L/s of Blazing Pyrotheum to run, which means that fluid needs to be automated before upgrading to Volcani; the main ways to do this are either to use the Pyrotheum Bee, or automatically mix coal"
- candidate `chunk-c525faf801bcb0fc5beef1a125d48446` doc=doc-04ef7ad9e1765bcf95cbd804c813863b words=2560-2960 distance=0.359078 similarity=0.640922 sections=[Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > UU-Matter Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > UU-Matter > Elemental Duplicator Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Cheaper Crystal Circuits Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Quality of Life Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Quality of Life > Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatch Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Quality of Life > Laser Vacuum Mirror] text="the game, particularly for circuits, nanites, and the Space Elevator. In order to obtain it in large quantities, the new Matter Fabrication CPU should be used once the player has a Quantum Anomaly to use to craft it. It has a free EU discount compared to its singleblock equivalent, access to parallels in addition to the existing perfect overclock all Mass Fabricators have, and the ability to use multiple Energy Hatches to scale better. It can also be used to produce Scrap and UU-Amplifier, but this is generally not as effective as overclocking more or placing more Matter Fabrication CPUs.\nElemental Duplicator\nThe Elemental Duplicator is the multiblock version of the Replicator, which can synthesize pure elements directly from UU-Matter. It is unlocked in UV, although it also requires a Quantum Anomaly in its recipe. It is most useful for certain rare elements, such as Oganesson, that are difficult to produce in sufficient quantities with other recipes.\nCheaper Crystal Circuits\nThe UV Energy Hatch unlocks a cheaper recipe for Crystalprocessors in the Circuit Assembly Line using Crystal SoCs. These SoCs can be made by engraving Crystal Processing Units, but it is far faster to make them from Ce:LuAG instead. There are two machines that can be used for Ce:LuAG: the Vacuum Furnace , which requires a loop, and the Industrial Autoclave , which requires Oganesson for the recipes without a chance of failure. Crystal SoCs will also be required in UHV for that tier's circuits.\nSidequests\nQuality of Life\nAuto-Taping Maintenance Hatch\nThe final maintenance upgrade in the game is the Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatch, which infinitely prevents all maintenance issues on multiblocks, without requiring any input at all. It also continuously fixes maintenance issues on connected multiblocks, meaning that it is no longer necessary to conduct maintenance on a multiblock before turning it on. Wallsharing can be useful in order to reduce the number of Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatches required for large arrays of multiblocks, and since there's never a need to access them, they can be placed in inaccessible locations in order to save on useful shared hatch space.\nLaser Vacuum Mirror\nThe Laser Vacuum Mirror is an upgraded laser pipe that can be used to rotate lasers , although merging or splitting them still requires an Active Transformer . It requires UHV circuits as well as Chromatic Glass, the latter being made in a Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver with a"

Duration: 1271 ms
Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?

Status: answer

Answer:

Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and double the total EU consumption, which quadruples EU/t usage (hence "2/4 overclocking"). Perfect overclocks instead quadruple the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same, which also quadruples EU/t usage (hence "4/4 overclocking").

Instead of this, the EHE(Extreme Heat Exchanger) can also be used to generate supercritical steam from the plasma, adding another step to the process but tripling the fuel efficiency. Duration: 1559 ms
Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?

Status: answer

Answer:

Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and double the total EU consumption, which quadruples EU/t usage (hence "2/4 overclocking"). Perfect overclocks instead quadruple the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same, which still quadruples EU/t usage (hence "4/4 overclocking").

- candidate `chunk-5e57a74464432107837c03099bfbc7b6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=785-971 distance=0.184034 similarity=0.815966 sections=[Electricity > Overclocking] text="Overclocking\nMain Article: Overclocking\nMachines of higher tiers can receive overclocks to speed up their recipes.\nRegular overclocks double the recipe's speed and total EU consumption, leading to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, overclocking is also called 2/4 overclocking.\nA perfect overclock instead quadruples the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same. This still leads to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, perfect overclocking is also called 4/4 overclocking.\nMachines typically receive one overclock per voltage tier above the minimum required for a recipe.\nSingleblock machines can only ever regular overclock.\nMultiblock machines perfect overclock on a case-by-case basis; their tooltips contain information on how to achieve perfect overclocks or upgrade overclocks to perfect overclocks. If no information is mentioned, they will regular overclock.\nMultiblocks with two energy hatches of the same voltage will always draw 4A to overclock a recipe to a tier higher than the energy hatch voltage (since 4A of the lower voltage contains the same EU as 1A of the higher voltage). This also allows them to run recipes with a minimum requirement of that higher voltage tier."

The current contents of the internal buffer can be checked with the Portable Scanner .\nThe maximum amount of amps a machine can draw is either listed on its tooltip or recipe-dependent. A machine can draw up to a maximum of ⌊ 2 × Recipe Usage EU/t Voltage Tier EU Limit ⌋ + 1 {\\displaystyle {\\displaystyle \\left\\lfloor {\\frac {2\\times {\\text{Recipe Usage EU/t}}}{\\text{Voltage Tier EU Limit}}}\\right\\rfloor +1}} amps to fill its internal buffer. - candidate `chunk-a8f441006abca56356cb8a5f143676d6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=0-71 distance=0.328075 similarity=0.671925 sections=[Electricity] text="The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. - candidate `chunk-569da83c1ca37e29f993fb2f4e71c7fa` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=333-453 distance=0.333953 similarity=0.666047 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="Voltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on."
- candidate `chunk-4f552df6ef7c8df800ed6524c02be6c5` doc=doc-a509849f031bb1dadb346a8565bf75e8 words=1156-1238 distance=0.344467 similarity=0.655533 sections=[Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Power] text="Power\nThe Eye of Harmony is extremely power-hungry, and will likely consume most of the player's power generation while they progress through its tiers. Without any overclocks its power usage is fairly modest, on the order of 100B EU/t, but it is also extremely slow, and adding even a single overclock increases it to multiple trillion EU/t due to its very inefficient overclocks. In UMV, there are three viable sources of power to run the Eye of Harmony and its supporting infrastructure."
- candidate `chunk-7d1135ad40ba2cc7dab530a017e5c5f6` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=1438-1498 distance=0.346981 similarity=0.653019 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Circuits] text="Circuits\nAfter the completion of the fusion reactor, it becomes possible to manufacture Crystal circuits. - candidate `chunk-13f2a5b1d10ed9bdd4d1926cef51033b` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=411-495 distance=0.349694 similarity=0.650306 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2] text="Fusion Reactor Mk2\nA Mk2 Fusion Reactor.\nThe Fusion Reactor Mk2 becomes available when the player is able to make Superdense Plates and ZPM Energy Hatches. It is also the final goal of ZPM, as it is required to make Americium, which is needed in large quantities for UV components. - candidate `chunk-47bd42d0723648a06b4d9ebfc6552d28` doc=doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2 words=3996-4336 distance=0.350248 similarity=0.649752 sections=[Power Generation > Fusion and Plasma] text="Fusion and Plasma\nSee More: Fusion Reactor\nFusion is unlocked in late LuV, opening the gate to ZPM and also to very powerful power generation. The Fusion Reactor is needed to create some new materials, but the plasma itself can give out a lot of EU if processed in the right machines. Not all the outputs of the reactor are plasmas, but the ones that are can all be used to generate power. Fusion reactors have unique 2/2 overclocks per tier.\nThe reactor itself needs a large, initial EU input to start working, and then needs additional energy while it processes the inputs into the outputs. If it ever stops, it will need the initial EU again to resume working. After getting it to work, the plasma can be moved into one of several machines. Plasma turbines convert it directly to EU and also output the molten version of the material that the plasma was made of. Large plasma turbine is available in LuV and XL plasma turbine is available in ZPM. Large plasma turbine does not accept tectech dynamo hatches while the XL one does. Instead of this, the EHE(Extreme Heat Exchanger) can also be used to generate supercritical steam from the plasma, adding another step to the process but tripling the fuel efficiency. While the EHE appears to be the superior option, it does not scale well, so it is only recommended to company regular fusion reactors and not compact fusion reactors.\nPlasmas that are commonly used for power generation are helium and tin plasma. Helium plasma produces 2,560,000 EU/t on a MK3 reactor (before turbine and EHE efficiency) and is generally preferred due to the source materials (Helium-3 and Deterium) being easily obtainable. Tin plasma produces 5,480,928 EU/t on a MK3 reactor and has the advantage of higher energy output and higher energy density (which is proportional to the maximum processing capability of EHE).\nBe warned that the XL Plasma Turbine does apply harsh penalties to plasmas with low energy density that run through good turbine blades."
- candidate `chunk-303f0acb1197f3638b42847847bb8637` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=1670-1836 distance=0.351707 similarity=0.648293 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Fusion Reactor Mk4] text="Fusion Reactor Mk4\nThe Mk4 Fusion Reactor is available in UHV, although it is not necessary for any recipes until UEV. Its primary advantage over previous tiers of Fusion Reactor is speed: unlike Mk2 or Mk3 Fusion Reactors, Mk4+ Fusion Reactors get 4/4 overclocks on recipes below their tier. This is still much slower than a Compact Mk3 when using the regular Mk4 Fusion Reactor, but the Compact Mk4 is a massive speed upgrade, ranging from 8 to 21 times as fast as a Compact Mk3 depending on the recipe tier.\nThe new recipes unlocked, other than a faster recipe for Molten Californium, are all for new materials: Fermium and Neptunium are used for the QFT , Rhugnor is mostly used for Hypogen, Hypogen is better produced through a loop in the DTPF , Metastable Oganesson is used for the Mk5 Fusion Reactor, Technetium Plasma is used in the Space Elevator, Bromine Plasma processes Europium and Americium combs, and Flerovium has almost no uses until UMV."

EU is also compatible with machines from Applied Energistics 2 and other machines that accept Redstone Flux (RF), converting at a rate of 1 EU to 3.6 RF. The reverse is not possible; RF cannot be converted to EU."
- candidate `chunk-569da83c1ca37e29f993fb2f4e71c7fa` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=333-453 distance=0.333953 similarity=0.666047 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="Voltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on."
- candidate `chunk-4f552df6ef7c8df800ed6524c02be6c5` doc=doc-a509849f031bb1dadb346a8565bf75e8 words=1156-1238 distance=0.344467 similarity=0.655533 sections=[Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Power] text="Power\nThe Eye of Harmony is extremely power-hungry, and will likely consume most of the player's power generation while they progress through its tiers. Without any overclocks its power usage is fairly modest, on the order of 100B EU/t, but it is also extremely slow, and adding even a single overclock increases it to multiple trillion EU/t due to its very inefficient overclocks. In UMV, there are three viable sources of power to run the Eye of Harmony and its supporting infrastructure."
- candidate `chunk-7d1135ad40ba2cc7dab530a017e5c5f6` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=1438-1498 distance=0.346981 similarity=0.653019 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Circuits] text="Circuits\nAfter the completion of the fusion reactor, it becomes possible to manufacture Crystal circuits. These circuits have a unique automation challenge due to how their \"CPU\" component is crafted; it requires a loop of autoclaving and forge hammering. In addition, the standard method of creating the CPUs requires molten europium. The Crystalprocessor Mainframe is the first UV circuit available."
- candidate `chunk-13f2a5b1d10ed9bdd4d1926cef51033b` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=411-495 distance=0.349694 similarity=0.650306 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2] text="Fusion Reactor Mk2\nA Mk2 Fusion Reactor.\nThe Fusion Reactor Mk2 becomes available when the player is able to make Superdense Plates and ZPM Energy Hatches. It is also the final goal of ZPM, as it is required to make Americium, which is needed in large quantities for UV components. In addition to the new recipes they have available, Mk2 fusion reactors can also run Mk1 recipes, which will result in a \"fusion overclock\", which uses twice the EU/t and works twice as fast."
- candidate `chunk-47bd42d0723648a06b4d9ebfc6552d28` doc=doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2 words=3996-4336 distance=0.350248 similarity=0.649752 sections=[Power Generation > Fusion and Plasma] text="Fusion and Plasma\nSee More: Fusion Reactor\nFusion is unlocked in late LuV, opening the gate to ZPM and also to very powerful power generation. The Fusion Reactor is needed to create some new materials, but the plasma itself can give out a lot of EU if processed in the right machines. Not all the outputs of the reactor are plasmas, but the ones that are can all be used to generate power. Fusion reactors have unique 2/2 overclocks per tier.\nThe reactor itself needs a large, initial EU input to start working, and then needs additional energy while it processes the inputs into the outputs. If it ever stops, it will need the initial EU again to resume working. After getting it to work, the plasma can be moved into one of several machines. Plasma turbines convert it directly to EU and also output the molten version of the material that the plasma was made of. Large plasma turbine is available in LuV and XL plasma turbine is available in ZPM. Large plasma turbine does not accept tectech dynamo hatches while the XL one does. Instead of this, the EHE(Extreme Heat Exchanger) can also be used to generate supercritical steam from the plasma, adding another step to the process but tripling the fuel efficiency. While the EHE appears to be the superior option, it does not scale well, so it is only recommended to company regular fusion reactors and not compact fusion reactors.\nPlasmas that are commonly used for power generation are helium and tin plasma. Helium plasma produces 2,560,000 EU/t on a MK3 reactor (before turbine and EHE efficiency) and is generally preferred due to the source materials (Helium-3 and Deterium) being easily obtainable. Tin plasma produces 5,480,928 EU/t on a MK3 reactor and has the advantage of higher energy output and higher energy density (which is proportional to the maximum processing capability of EHE).\nBe warned that the XL Plasma Turbine does apply harsh penalties to plasmas with low energy density that run through good turbine blades."
- candidate `chunk-303f0acb1197f3638b42847847bb8637` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=1670-1836 distance=0.351707 similarity=0.648293 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Fusion Reactor Mk4] text="Fusion Reactor Mk4\nThe Mk4 Fusion Reactor is available in UHV, although it is not necessary for any recipes until UEV. Its primary advantage over previous tiers of Fusion Reactor is speed: unlike Mk2 or Mk3 Fusion Reactors, Mk4+ Fusion Reactors get 4/4 overclocks on recipes below their tier. This is still much slower than a Compact Mk3 when using the regular Mk4 Fusion Reactor, but the Compact Mk4 is a massive speed upgrade, ranging from 8 to 21 times as fast as a Compact Mk3 depending on the recipe tier.\nThe new recipes unlocked, other than a faster recipe for Molten Californium, are all for new materials: Fermium and Neptunium are used for the QFT , Rhugnor is mostly used for Hypogen, Hypogen is better produced through a loop in the DTPF , Metastable Oganesson is used for the Mk5 Fusion Reactor, Technetium Plasma is used in the Space Elevator, Bromine Plasma processes Europium and Americium combs, and Flerovium has almost no uses until UMV."
- context `chunk-5e57a74464432107837c03099bfbc7b6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=785-971 text="Overclocking\nMain Article: Overclocking\nMachines of higher tiers can receive overclocks to speed up their recipes.\nRegular overclocks double the recipe's speed and total EU consumption, leading to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, overclocking is also called 2/4 overclocking.\nA perfect overclock instead quadruples the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same. This still leads to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, perfect overclocking is also called 4/4 overclocking.\nMachines typically receive one overclock per voltage tier above the minimum required for a recipe.\nSingleblock machines can only ever regular overclock.\nMultiblock machines perfect overclock on a case-by-case basis; their tooltips contain information on how to achieve perfect overclocks or upgrade overclocks to perfect overclocks. If no information is mentioned, they will regular overclock.\nMultiblocks with two energy hatches of the same voltage will always draw 4A to overclock a recipe to a tier higher than the energy hatch voltage (since 4A of the lower voltage contains the same EU as 1A of the higher voltage). This also allows them to run recipes with a minimum requirement of that higher voltage tier."

- context `chunk-268950b23008748d06a2400f6acdb574` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=453-785 text="Amperage\nIn code, amps are pushed, not pulled. ## filtered-rewritten / q01

Question: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- A regular overclock doubles recipe speed, doubles total EU consumption, and therefore quadruples EU/t.
- A perfect overclock quadruples recipe speed while keeping total EU consumption unchanged, and therefore quadruples EU/t.
- expected source doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0/section-edab5ff0194600b58b19dce3fb2eaf62

Duration: 1456 ms
Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?

Status: answer

Answer:

Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and double the total EU consumption, which quadruples EU/t usage (hence "2/4 overclocking"). Perfect overclocks instead quadruple the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same, which also quadruples EU/t usage (hence "4/4 overclocking").

Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: GregTech New Horizons regular overclock vs perfect overclock recipe speed EU/t total energy difference

Status: answer

Answer:

Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and double the total EU consumption, which quadruples EU/t usage (hence "2/4 overclocking"). Perfect overclocks instead quadruple the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same, which also quadruples EU/t usage (hence "4/4 overclocking").

Note that machines can request more Amperage than strictly required by their active recipe.\n- Each energy packet travelling through a cable loses Voltage per block travelled. Note that Uninsulated Wires have twice the Loss/Meter/Ampere as Insulated Cables. Four generators on the same cable will output 32 volts in 4 amps combined. 32 volts in 4 amps is not the same thing as MV (Medium Voltage - 128 volts per amp). This can be compared to four cables containing 32 volts each, or one 4x Cable. The x rating of a cable (x1, x2, x4, etc.) denotes its maximum amperage. The general rule of thumb is your cables should have an equal Amp capacity to the number of generators/batteries attached. Battery Buffers output 1A per battery , while virtually every generator puts out 1A. - candidate `chunk-268950b23008748d06a2400f6acdb574` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=453-785 distance=0.327669 similarity=0.672331 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Amperage] text="Amperage\nIn code, amps are pushed, not pulled. However, they are only pushed when requested by machines. Thus, for all scopes except pack development, you can assume amps are only ever pulled as needed.\nMachines and energy hatches draw amps to fill their internal EU buffers. The capacity of the internal buffer is listed as \"Capacity:\" in the machine's or hatch's tooltip. When processing a recipe, a machine will draw from its internal buffer. The current contents of the internal buffer can be checked with the Portable Scanner .\nThe maximum amount of amps a machine can draw is either listed on its tooltip or recipe-dependent. A machine can draw up to a maximum of ⌊ 2 × Recipe Usage EU/t Voltage Tier EU Limit ⌋ + 1 {\\displaystyle {\\displaystyle \\left\\lfloor {\\frac {2\\times {\\text{Recipe Usage EU/t}}}{\\text{Voltage Tier EU Limit}}}\\right\\rfloor +1}} amps to fill its internal buffer. This means that if the machine isn't processing a recipe, it will draw 1 amp to refill the internal buffer. Recipe amperages listed in NEI are a recommended number to fill the internal buffer at a rate that breaks even against usage.\nSeveral common amperages of GregTech machines can be found in the table below. \"Drawing\" means \"draws up to\", unless otherwise stated.\nOutput amps contain the maximum EU for the outputting machine's voltage tier.\nMachine | Notes\nMachine: Singleblock Generators | Notes: Output 1A of its tier\nMachine: Energy Hatches | Notes: Draws 2A (second amp mostly for extra draw for loss)\nMachine: Step-up Transformers | Notes: Draws 4A lower voltage, outputs 1A higher voltage\nMachine: Step-down Transformers | Notes: Draws 1A higher voltage, outputs 4A lower voltage\nMachine: Battery Buffers | Notes: Draws 2A per Battery, outputs 1A per Battery.\nMachine: Battery Chargers | Notes: Draws 4-8A per Battery, outputs 2-4A per Battery correspondingly.\nMachine: Arc Furnace | Notes: Most recipes require 3A to break even against EU/t usage\nMachine: Thermal Centrifuge | Notes: Most recipes require 2A to break even against EU/t usage"
- candidate `chunk-a8f441006abca56356cb8a5f143676d6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=0-71 distance=0.328075 similarity=0.671925 sections=[Electricity] text="The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. EU is used to run GregTech and IC2 machines. Every Tier offers multiple types of Power Generation options at LV and above. EU is also compatible with machines from Applied Energistics 2 and other machines that accept Redstone Flux (RF), converting at a rate of 1 EU to 3.6 RF. The reverse is not possible; RF cannot be converted to EU."
- candidate `chunk-569da83c1ca37e29f993fb2f4e71c7fa` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=333-453 distance=0.333953 similarity=0.666047 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="Voltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on."
- candidate `chunk-4f552df6ef7c8df800ed6524c02be6c5` doc=doc-a509849f031bb1dadb346a8565bf75e8 words=1156-1238 distance=0.344467 similarity=0.655533 sections=[Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Power] text="Power\nThe Eye of Harmony is extremely power-hungry, and will likely consume most of the player's power generation while they progress through its tiers. Without any overclocks its power usage is fairly modest, on the order of 100B EU/t, but it is also extremely slow, and adding even a single overclock increases it to multiple trillion EU/t due to its very inefficient overclocks. In UMV, there are three viable sources of power to run the Eye of Harmony and its supporting infrastructure."
- candidate `chunk-7d1135ad40ba2cc7dab530a017e5c5f6` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=1438-1498 distance=0.346981 similarity=0.653019 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Circuits] text="Circuits\nAfter the completion of the fusion reactor, it becomes possible to manufacture Crystal circuits. These circuits have a unique automation challenge due to how their \"CPU\" component is crafted; it requires a loop of autoclaving and forge hammering. In addition, the standard method of creating the CPUs requires molten europium. The Crystalprocessor Mainframe is the first UV circuit available."
- candidate `chunk-13f2a5b1d10ed9bdd4d1926cef51033b` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=411-495 distance=0.349694 similarity=0.650306 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2] text="Fusion Reactor Mk2\nA Mk2 Fusion Reactor.\nThe Fusion Reactor Mk2 becomes available when the player is able to make Superdense Plates and ZPM Energy Hatches. It is also the final goal of ZPM, as it is required to make Americium, which is needed in large quantities for UV components. In addition to the new recipes they have available, Mk2 fusion reactors can also run Mk1 recipes, which will result in a \"fusion overclock\", which uses twice the EU/t and works twice as fast."
- candidate `chunk-47bd42d0723648a06b4d9ebfc6552d28` doc=doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2 words=3996-4336 distance=0.350248 similarity=0.649752 sections=[Power Generation > Fusion and Plasma] text="Fusion and Plasma\nSee More: Fusion Reactor\nFusion is unlocked in late LuV, opening the gate to ZPM and also to very powerful power generation. The Fusion Reactor is needed to create some new materials, but the plasma itself can give out a lot of EU if processed in the right machines. Not all the outputs of the reactor are plasmas, but the ones that are can all be used to generate power. Fusion reactors have unique 2/2 overclocks per tier.\nThe reactor itself needs a large, initial EU input to start working, and then needs additional energy while it processes the inputs into the outputs. If it ever stops, it will need the initial EU again to resume working. After getting it to work, the plasma can be moved into one of several machines. Plasma turbines convert it directly to EU and also output the molten version of the material that the plasma was made of. Large plasma turbine is available in LuV and XL plasma turbine is available in ZPM. Large plasma turbine does not accept tectech dynamo hatches while the XL one does. Instead of this, the EHE(Extreme Heat Exchanger) can also be used to generate supercritical steam from the plasma, adding another step to the process but tripling the fuel efficiency. While the EHE appears to be the superior option, it does not scale well, so it is only recommended to company regular fusion reactors and not compact fusion reactors.\nPlasmas that are commonly used for power generation are helium and tin plasma. Helium plasma produces 2,560,000 EU/t on a MK3 reactor (before turbine and EHE efficiency) and is generally preferred due to the source materials (Helium-3 and Deterium) being easily obtainable. Tin plasma produces 5,480,928 EU/t on a MK3 reactor and has the advantage of higher energy output and higher energy density (which is proportional to the maximum processing capability of EHE).\nBe warned that the XL Plasma Turbine does apply harsh penalties to plasmas with low energy density that run through good turbine blades."
- candidate `chunk-303f0acb1197f3638b42847847bb8637` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=1670-1836 distance=0.351707 similarity=0.648293 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Fusion Reactor Mk4] text="Fusion Reactor Mk4\nThe Mk4 Fusion Reactor is available in UHV, although it is not necessary for any recipes until UEV. Its primary advantage over previous tiers of Fusion Reactor is speed: unlike Mk2 or Mk3 Fusion Reactors, Mk4+ Fusion Reactors get 4/4 overclocks on recipes below their tier. This is still much slower than a Compact Mk3 when using the regular Mk4 Fusion Reactor, but the Compact Mk4 is a massive speed upgrade, ranging from 8 to 21 times as fast as a Compact Mk3 depending on the recipe tier.\nThe new recipes unlocked, other than a faster recipe for Molten Californium, are all for new materials: Fermium and Neptunium are used for the QFT , Rhugnor is mostly used for Hypogen, Hypogen is better produced through a loop in the DTPF , Metastable Oganesson is used for the Mk5 Fusion Reactor, Technetium Plasma is used in the Space Elevator, Bromine Plasma processes Europium and Americium combs, and Flerovium has almost no uses until UMV."

Duration: 1372 ms
Original query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?
Search query: How do regular and perfect overclocks differ in recipe speed, EU/t and total energy?

Status: answer

Answer:

Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and total EU consumption, leading to quadrupled EU/t usage (hence called 2/4 overclocking). Perfect overclocks instead quadruple the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same, which still leads to quadrupled EU/t usage (hence called 4/4 overclocking).

Original query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?
Search query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?

Status: answer

Answer:

In GregTech: New Horizons, an LV Combustion Generator (the small combustion generator) produces 1 amp of LV power (32 EU/t) but consumes fuel at a rate corresponding to a higher internal EU value. Specifically, it generates 32 EU/t output while internally burning fuel for 40 EU/t, meaning 8 EU/t is lost as inefficiency. This is a 20% loss, so the generator effectively draws 40 EU/t worth of fuel energy to output 32 EU/t (1 amp of LV).

This can be compared to four cables containing 32 volts each, or one 4x Cable. The x rating of a cable (x1, x2, x4, etc.) denotes its maximum amperage. - candidate `chunk-33506a46db8cb160a686236470dc2d56` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=351-524 distance=0.306822 similarity=0.693178 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Loss] text="Energy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible."

Original query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?
Search query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?

Status: answer

Answer:

An LV Combustion Generator draws 33 EU from its internal buffer to output 1 amp holding 32 EU, so the energy lost is 1 EU.

- candidate `chunk-268950b23008748d06a2400f6acdb574` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=453-785 distance=0.280846 similarity=0.719154 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Amperage] text="Amperage\nIn code, amps are pushed, not pulled. However, they are only pushed when requested by machines. Thus, for all scopes except pack development, you can assume amps are only ever pulled as needed.\nMachines and energy hatches draw amps to fill their internal EU buffers. The capacity of the internal buffer is listed as \"Capacity:\" in the machine's or hatch's tooltip. When processing a recipe, a machine will draw from its internal buffer. The current contents of the internal buffer can be checked with the Portable Scanner .\nThe maximum amount of amps a machine can draw is either listed on its tooltip or recipe-dependent. A machine can draw up to a maximum of ⌊ 2 × Recipe Usage EU/t Voltage Tier EU Limit ⌋ + 1 {\\displaystyle {\\displaystyle \\left\\lfloor {\\frac {2\\times {\\text{Recipe Usage EU/t}}}{\\text{Voltage Tier EU Limit}}}\\right\\rfloor +1}} amps to fill its internal buffer. This means that if the machine isn't processing a recipe, it will draw 1 amp to refill the internal buffer. Recipe amperages listed in NEI are a recommended number to fill the internal buffer at a rate that breaks even against usage.\nSeveral common amperages of GregTech machines can be found in the table below. \"Drawing\" means \"draws up to\", unless otherwise stated.\nOutput amps contain the maximum EU for the outputting machine's voltage tier.\nMachine | Notes\nMachine: Singleblock Generators | Notes: Output 1A of its tier\nMachine: Energy Hatches | Notes: Draws 2A (second amp mostly for extra draw for loss)\nMachine: Step-up Transformers | Notes: Draws 4A lower voltage, outputs 1A higher voltage\nMachine: Step-down Transformers | Notes: Draws 1A higher voltage, outputs 4A lower voltage\nMachine: Battery Buffers | Notes: Draws 2A per Battery, outputs 1A per Battery.\nMachine: Battery Chargers | Notes: Draws 4-8A per Battery, outputs 2-4A per Battery correspondingly.\nMachine: Arc Furnace | Notes: Most recipes require 3A to break even against EU/t usage\nMachine: Thermal Centrifuge | Notes: Most recipes require 2A to break even against EU/t usage"

- context `chunk-7377a2351dcc2bc55102f8f2bc69e9e2` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=201-351 text="EU (Energy Units) Mechanics\nGregTech energy consists of Voltage and Amperage. - candidate `chunk-569da83c1ca37e29f993fb2f4e71c7fa` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=333-453 distance=0.301582 similarity=0.698418 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="Voltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on."
- candidate `chunk-33506a46db8cb160a686236470dc2d56` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=351-524 distance=0.306822 similarity=0.693178 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Loss] text="Energy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible."
- candidate `chunk-66d85c9407fba7874f8f63f6e9f54ea5` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=71-312 distance=0.310052 similarity=0.689948 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage] text="Voltage and Amperage\nAcronym | Voltage Tier | EU Limit\nAcronym: ULV | Voltage Tier: Ultra Low Voltage | EU Limit: 8\nAcronym: LV | Voltage Tier: Low Voltage | EU Limit: 32\nAcronym: MV | Voltage Tier: Medium Voltage | EU Limit: 128\nAcronym: HV | Voltage Tier: High Voltage | EU Limit: 512\nAcronym: EV | Voltage Tier: Extreme Voltage | EU Limit: 2,048\nAcronym: IV | Voltage Tier: Insane Voltage | EU Limit: 8,192\nAcronym: LuV | Voltage Tier: Ludicrous Voltage | EU Limit: 32,768\nAcronym: ZPM | Voltage Tier: ZPM Voltage | EU Limit: 131,072\nAcronym: UV | Voltage Tier: Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 524,288\nAcronym: UHV | Voltage Tier: Highly Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 2,097,152\nAcronym: UEV | Voltage Tier: Extremely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 8,388,608\nAcronym: UIV | Voltage Tier: Insanely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 33,554,432\nAcronym: UMV | Voltage Tier: Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 134,217,728\nAcronym: UXV | Voltage Tier: Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 536,870,912\nAcronym: MAX | Voltage Tier: Maximum Voltage | EU Limit: 2,147,483,648\nEU in GregTech comes in a system of Voltage (Volts, V) and Amperage (Amps, A).\nEnergy is transferred in packages. Voltage describes the size of the energy packages, while Amperage describes the number of packages. When you multiply both, you get the power in EU/t (Energy Units per tick), which describes the energy produced, transferred, or consumed over time."

This means that if the machine isn't processing a recipe, it will draw 1 amp to refill the internal buffer. Original query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?
Search query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?

Status: answer

Answer:

An LV Combustion Generator draws 33 EU from its internal buffer to output 1 amp holding 32 EU, so 1 EU is lost.

- candidate `chunk-569da83c1ca37e29f993fb2f4e71c7fa` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=333-453 distance=0.301582 similarity=0.698418 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="Voltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on."
- candidate `chunk-33506a46db8cb160a686236470dc2d56` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=351-524 distance=0.306822 similarity=0.693178 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Loss] text="Energy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible."
- candidate `chunk-66d85c9407fba7874f8f63f6e9f54ea5` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=71-312 distance=0.310052 similarity=0.689948 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage] text="Voltage and Amperage\nAcronym | Voltage Tier | EU Limit\nAcronym: ULV | Voltage Tier: Ultra Low Voltage | EU Limit: 8\nAcronym: LV | Voltage Tier: Low Voltage | EU Limit: 32\nAcronym: MV | Voltage Tier: Medium Voltage | EU Limit: 128\nAcronym: HV | Voltage Tier: High Voltage | EU Limit: 512\nAcronym: EV | Voltage Tier: Extreme Voltage | EU Limit: 2,048\nAcronym: IV | Voltage Tier: Insane Voltage | EU Limit: 8,192\nAcronym: LuV | Voltage Tier: Ludicrous Voltage | EU Limit: 32,768\nAcronym: ZPM | Voltage Tier: ZPM Voltage | EU Limit: 131,072\nAcronym: UV | Voltage Tier: Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 524,288\nAcronym: UHV | Voltage Tier: Highly Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 2,097,152\nAcronym: UEV | Voltage Tier: Extremely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 8,388,608\nAcronym: UIV | Voltage Tier: Insanely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 33,554,432\nAcronym: UMV | Voltage Tier: Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 134,217,728\nAcronym: UXV | Voltage Tier: Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 536,870,912\nAcronym: MAX | Voltage Tier: Maximum Voltage | EU Limit: 2,147,483,648\nEU in GregTech comes in a system of Voltage (Volts, V) and Amperage (Amps, A).\nEnergy is transferred in packages. Voltage describes the size of the energy packages, while Amperage describes the number of packages. When you multiply both, you get the power in EU/t (Energy Units per tick), which describes the energy produced, transferred, or consumed over time."
- candidate `chunk-137405157af87dd0f3eee24e6971f51d` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=643-1043 distance=0.320950 similarity=0.679050 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > GT Electric Machines] text="GT Electric Machines\nMachine GUI. Auto-output buttons circled in yellow.\nLV Electric machines have some new features that were not available with Steam-age machinery. For example, the steam exhaust is replaced with an automatic output. This output's facing can be changed with a wrench similar to how the exhaust was configured on Steam machines. Just like their Steam counterparts, all electric GT machines cannot be input or output from their front face. To enable automatic output, open the GUI of the machine and click on the button at the lower left corner. There are two automatic output toggle buttons; the left one is for liquid and the right one is for items.\nElectrolyzer clay dust recipe. The MV power requirement is circled in yellow.\nGregTech machinery is divided by tier, which corresponds to a specific voltage - LV (32 V), MV (128 V), HV (512 V) etc. Most recipes are gated to a specific voltage/tier or higher, which is shown with the recipe in NEI (Not Enough Items). If the recipe requires more than one amp it will also be listed here. Pay careful attention to what tier a recipe requires - with LV machinery, MV and higher recipes are inaccessible.\nFor example, putting Clay Dust through the Electrolyzer to get Aluminium dust requires 120 EU/t (MV). Since the Basic Electrolyzer is only able to do 32EU/t, this recipe is unavailable until the Advanced Electrolyzer (MV).\nRecipes close to the voltage limit for LV (32 EU/t) may cause the machine to request multiple amps, especially if there is any cable loss. A single LV generator will often not be capable of supplying enough power if the machine is placed too far away. Most GT machines will accept up to 2 amps. A second generator or Battery Buffer may be needed to keep a a high cost recipe running. If a machine runs out of power, it will stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.\nSome machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . The Arc Furnace requires 3 amps to function and can accept up to 7 amps. Checking any recipe for the Arc Furnace will show Usage XX/t, voltage 32 EU/t"
- candidate `chunk-31999df98437a688bc59ee797433641e` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=266-412 distance=0.323036 similarity=0.676964 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > First Energy Crisis] text="First Energy Crisis\nYou may find yourself struggling to power HV EBFs and possibly even your singleblock machines for long periods of time, as each HV machine you make consumes 4x (not accounting for efficiency loss) the amount of fuel compared to your MV generators. You should expand and fully automate your energy production setup.\nIn HV, combustion generators gain a massive buff thanks to the addition of Cetane-Boosted Diesel, which boasts a whopping 1M EU per cell, a massive expansion over Diesel. In addition, Benzene is heavily improved thanks to the Distillation Tower and Pyrolyse Oven coil upgrades which significantly speed up Benzene production. The Distillation Tower will even produce Phenol and Toluene which can be burned in Gas Turbines if you're in a pinch. Note that these infrastructure upgrades require significant amounts of resources upfront, but the infrastructure investment easily carries over into EV."
- candidate `chunk-a8f441006abca56356cb8a5f143676d6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=0-71 distance=0.326881 similarity=0.673119 sections=[Electricity] text="The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. EU is used to run GregTech and IC2 machines. Every Tier offers multiple types of Power Generation options at LV and above. EU is also compatible with machines from Applied Energistics 2 and other machines that accept Redstone Flux (RF), converting at a rate of 1 EU to 3.6 RF. The reverse is not possible; RF cannot be converted to EU."
- candidate `chunk-df7fb1d7f5beb071b0f8ad99ef260a9b` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=4191-4395 distance=0.328028 similarity=0.671972 sections=[Electricity > Transformers] text="Transformers\nPicture of a Transformer in default mode transferring 1 amp of HV into 4 amps of MV.\nTransformers convert EU between voltage tiers. In Step Up mode, they draw up to 4 amps of a lower voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce 1A of a higher voltage. This can allow lower tier amps to power higher tier machines which may only draw 1-2 A for a recipe. Similarly, in Step Down mode, they draw 1 amp of a higher voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce up to 4A of a lower voltage. This allows use of higher tier power generators with lower tier machines while preventing explosions. Use a Soft Mallet to switch the mode.\nThe big dot with a plus is the high voltage side and is the front face, while the five smaller circles are the lower voltage sides. Regardless of mode, the big dot is always for the higher voltage. That means in Step Up mode, transformers have one output, five inputs, and in Step Down mode, they have five outputs, one input.\nThe output loss section above applies to transformer outputs as well."

- candidate `chunk-33506a46db8cb160a686236470dc2d56` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=351-524 distance=0.306822 similarity=0.693178 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Loss] text="Energy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible."

Duration: 2934 ms
Original query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?
Search query: GregTech New Horizons LV Combustion Generator internal EU draw per amp output and EU loss

Status: answer

Answer:

An LV Combustion Generator draws 33 EU from its internal buffer to output one amp holding 32 EU, so 1 EU is lost. This matches the general formula: a power-outputting singleblock draws 8 × 4^tier + 2^max(0, tier−1) EU from its internal buffer and outputs 8 × 4^tier EU. For LV (tier 1), that is 8 × 4 + 2^0 = 33 EU consumed, 32 EU output, and 2^max(0, 1−1) = 1 EU lost.

- candidate `chunk-a8f441006abca56356cb8a5f143676d6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=0-71 distance=0.288060 similarity=0.711940 sections=[Electricity] text="The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. - candidate `chunk-fdf371b1592b7ed0250bf63b741b8cb9` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=971-1371 distance=0.299641 similarity=0.700359 sections=[Electricity > Cables and Loss] text="Cables and Loss\nGregTech EU can be transferred using GregTech Cables.\nRather than priority by destination, power priority is given by cardinal direction. This can cause one generator in a cable network to use fuel more rapidly than another, with order depending on tile entity processing and changing on chunk reloads.\nAll GT Cables have a max Voltage, max Amperage and a Loss/Meter/Ampere, indicated on their tooltip:\n- Cables which receive amps containing more EU than their maximum Voltage will catch fire and melt.\n- Cables that have more amps travelling through them than their maximum Amperage limit will catch fire and melt. Note that machines can request more Amperage than strictly required by their active recipe.\n- Each energy packet travelling through a cable loses Voltage per block travelled. The amount of EU lost is indicated by the Loss/Meter/Ampere number.\nEach Material has 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x, and 16x uninsulated Wires. Most of these have cable variants, except for the superconductor wires, as well as graphene, Ichorium, hypogen, Black Plutonium, Awakened Draconium, Infinity, and SpaceTime wires. Note that Uninsulated Wires have twice the Loss/Meter/Ampere as Insulated Cables. The only exceptions to this are Red alloy and Redstone alloy (as their cables are lossless, while the wires are not), Quantium, Lumiium, and Signalium (four times the loss when uninsulated), and Bedrockium (8x loss when uninsulated).\nFor example:\n- A 1x Tin Cable can handle 1A containing 32EU at a loss of 1 EU-Volt/Meter/Ampere. This means that 1 amp can travel 32 blocks before it dies.\n- A 1x Tin Wire can handle 1A containing 32EU at a loss of 2 EU-Volt/Meter/Ampere. In this case, the amp can travel 16 blocks only.\nBelow is a table of the current properties of various types of cables in GregTech: Note: In 2.8.0, many cables received maximum amperage and loss changes. This table is accurate as of version 2.8.1+.\nMaterial | Max Voltage [ 1 ] | Amp [ 2 ] | Loss [ 3 ] | Decay [ 4 ]\nMaterial: Tin | Max Voltage [ 1 ]: LV (32) | Amp [ 2 ]: 1 | Loss [ 3 ]: 1 | Decay ["

- candidate `chunk-33506a46db8cb160a686236470dc2d56` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=351-524 distance=0.306822 similarity=0.693178 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Loss] text="Energy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible."
- candidate `chunk-66d85c9407fba7874f8f63f6e9f54ea5` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=71-312 distance=0.310052 similarity=0.689948 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage] text="Voltage and Amperage\nAcronym | Voltage Tier | EU Limit\nAcronym: ULV | Voltage Tier: Ultra Low Voltage | EU Limit: 8\nAcronym: LV | Voltage Tier: Low Voltage | EU Limit: 32\nAcronym: MV | Voltage Tier: Medium Voltage | EU Limit: 128\nAcronym: HV | Voltage Tier: High Voltage | EU Limit: 512\nAcronym: EV | Voltage Tier: Extreme Voltage | EU Limit: 2,048\nAcronym: IV | Voltage Tier: Insane Voltage | EU Limit: 8,192\nAcronym: LuV | Voltage Tier: Ludicrous Voltage | EU Limit: 32,768\nAcronym: ZPM | Voltage Tier: ZPM Voltage | EU Limit: 131,072\nAcronym: UV | Voltage Tier: Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 524,288\nAcronym: UHV | Voltage Tier: Highly Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 2,097,152\nAcronym: UEV | Voltage Tier: Extremely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 8,388,608\nAcronym: UIV | Voltage Tier: Insanely Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 33,554,432\nAcronym: UMV | Voltage Tier: Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 134,217,728\nAcronym: UXV | Voltage Tier: Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage | EU Limit: 536,870,912\nAcronym: MAX | Voltage Tier: Maximum Voltage | EU Limit: 2,147,483,648\nEU in GregTech comes in a system of Voltage (Volts, V) and Amperage (Amps, A).\nEnergy is transferred in packages.
