Auto-output buttons circled in yellow.\nLV Electric machines have some new features that were not available with Steam-age machinery. For example, the steam exhaust is replaced with an automatic output. This output's facing can be changed with a wrench similar to how the exhaust was configured on Steam machines. Just like their Steam counterparts, all electric GT machines cannot be input or output from their front face. To enable automatic output, open the GUI of the machine and click on the button at the lower left corner. There are two automatic output toggle buttons; the left one is for liquid and the right one is for items.\nElectrolyzer clay dust recipe. The MV power requirement is circled in yellow.\nGregTech machinery is divided by tier, which corresponds to a specific voltage - LV (32 V), MV (128 V), HV (512 V) etc. Most recipes are gated to a specific voltage/tier or higher, which is shown with the recipe in NEI (Not Enough Items). Pay careful attention to what tier a recipe requires - with LV machinery, MV and higher recipes are inaccessible.\nFor example, putting Clay Dust through the Electrolyzer to get Aluminium dust requires 120 EU/t (MV). A second generator or Battery Buffer may be needed to keep a a high cost recipe running. If a machine runs out of power, it will stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.\nSome machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . - candidate `chunk-31999df98437a688bc59ee797433641e` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=266-412 distance=0.323036 similarity=0.676964 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > First Energy Crisis] text="First Energy Crisis\nYou may find yourself struggling to power HV EBFs and possibly even your singleblock machines for long periods of time, as each HV machine you make consumes 4x (not accounting for efficiency loss) the amount of fuel compared to your MV generators. The Distillation Tower will even produce Phenol and Toluene which can be burned in Gas Turbines if you're in a pinch. - candidate `chunk-a8f441006abca56356cb8a5f143676d6` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=0-71 distance=0.326881 similarity=0.673119 sections=[Electricity] text="The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. EU is used to run GregTech and IC2 machines. Every Tier offers multiple types of Power Generation options at LV and above. EU is also compatible with machines from Applied Energistics 2 and other machines that accept Redstone Flux (RF), converting at a rate of 1 EU to 3.6 RF. The reverse is not possible; RF cannot be converted to EU."
- candidate `chunk-df7fb1d7f5beb071b0f8ad99ef260a9b` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=4191-4395 distance=0.328028 similarity=0.671972 sections=[Electricity > Transformers] text="Transformers\nPicture of a Transformer in default mode transferring 1 amp of HV into 4 amps of MV.\nTransformers convert EU between voltage tiers. In Step Up mode, they draw up to 4 amps of a lower voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce 1A of a higher voltage. This can allow lower tier amps to power higher tier machines which may only draw 1-2 A for a recipe. Similarly, in Step Down mode, they draw 1 amp of a higher voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce up to 4A of a lower voltage. This allows use of higher tier power generators with lower tier machines while preventing explosions. Use a Soft Mallet to switch the mode.\nThe big dot with a plus is the high voltage side and is the front face, while the five smaller circles are the lower voltage sides. Regardless of mode, the big dot is always for the higher voltage. That means in Step Up mode, transformers have one output, five inputs, and in Step Down mode, they have five outputs, one input.\nThe output loss section above applies to transformer outputs as well."

- context `chunk-7377a2351dcc2bc55102f8f2bc69e9e2` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=201-351 text="EU (Energy Units) Mechanics\nGregTech energy consists of Voltage and Amperage. A Low Voltage (LV) GT generator will output 32 volts (32V) in 1 amperage (1A/1 amp). Four generators on the same cable will output 32 volts in 4 amps combined. 32 volts in 4 amps is not the same thing as MV (Medium Voltage - 128 volts per amp). This can be compared to four cables containing 32 volts each, or one 4x Cable. The x rating of a cable (x1, x2, x4, etc.) denotes its maximum amperage. The general rule of thumb is your cables should have an equal Amp capacity to the number of generators/batteries attached. Battery Buffers output 1A per battery , while virtually every generator puts out 1A. Having a cable with enough Amperage capacity for all of them at once prevents fires and explosions .\nFor more advanced and complete information, see Electricity ."
- context `chunk-268950b23008748d06a2400f6acdb574` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=453-785 text="Amperage\nIn code, amps are pushed, not pulled. Original query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?
Search query: How much EU does an LV Combustion Generator draw internally to output one amp, and how much is lost?

Status: answer

Answer:

An LV Combustion Generator draws 33 EU from its internal buffer to output 1 amp holding 32 EU. The energy lost is therefore 1 EU (3.0303%).

- candidate `chunk-569da83c1ca37e29f993fb2f4e71c7fa` doc=doc-3dbc9b7b97cfc0b8fbe14bc95a57ccc0 words=333-453 distance=0.301582 similarity=0.698418 sections=[Electricity > Voltage and Amperage > Voltage Tiers] text="Voltage Tiers\nMain Article: Tier\nGregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .\nThe EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.\nNote: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on."
- candidate `chunk-33506a46db8cb160a686236470dc2d56` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=351-524 distance=0.306822 similarity=0.693178 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Loss] text="Energy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible."

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In an MV EnderIO ore-processing setup, the priority order is usually: (1) Override, (2) Default, (3) Output. The SAG Mill or other processing machine has an 'Override' input slot that takes precedence over the normal 'Default' input slot; if an item is present in Override, it is processed instead of the Default input. The 'Output' slot is where the processed result is placed and is not an input priority. In practice, for a central ore-processing line, you route ores into the Default input for normal processing, use the Override input only for special cases or manual overrides, and extract finished products from the Output slot. If you are using conduits or item routing, set the machine's input side to accept into Default, and use the Override slot only when you want to force a specific recipe or item to be handled first.

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "Central Line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores or rare earths), Priority -1 for type filter routes (the default paths taken if nothing overrides them), and Priority -2 for output routes going to the final output chest.

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "central line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.), Priority -1 for type filter routes (the default paths taken if nothing overrides them), and Priority -2 for output routes (going to the final output chest).

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "Central Line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores or rare earths), Priority -1 for type filter routes (the default paths taken if nothing overrides them), and Priority -2 for output routes going to the final output chest.

It is able to process thousands of ores per second, and can do every step of ore processing in one machine, making it much faster, more scalable, and more performant than previous ore processing setups. Even with these benefits, it can often struggle to keep up with high-tier Space Elevator mining modules, requiring parallelization, overclocking with 2, 8, or even 32 energy hatches, or both. The IOF should be the only ore processor in lategame bases."

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "Central Line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores or rare earths), Priority -1 for type filter routes, which are the default paths taken if nothing overrides them, and Priority -2 for output routes, which go to the final output chest.

As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:\n- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)\n- Maceration Stack (MS)\n- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium\n- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices,"

This involves ME Storage Buses with the appropriate definitions as above, facing towards an ME interface linked to your main AE Network.\n- (Optional) Setup an Overflow. The overflow should be a storage bus with minimum priority but with no definitions at all. Any items that is not supposed to go to output but does not have anywhere else to go (because all the input busses are full) should go here, and should be pushed back into the Input. (This is only needed if your system cannot process all the materials fast enough, and if you usually have some downtime between ore-processing batches, which is common in EV/IV. By replacing the conventional input bus with an Advanced Stocking Input Bus with auto-pull enabled, there's no need to store directly into an Input Bus, so the throughput is not limited by filling up said input bus. Advanced Stocking Input Buses can also be used to run recipe checks whenever their contents change, avoiding downtime due to recipe switches. This improvement is effectively necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. - candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.343650 similarity=0.656350 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

- candidate `chunk-c8e59522b3ff87a5d0822136802a4e00` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=1513-1608 distance=0.347877 similarity=0.652123 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Integrated Ore Factory] text="Integrated Ore Factory\nThe Integrated Ore Factory is a large-scale ore processing multiblock that is unlocked with UEV circuits. It is able to process thousands of ores per second, and can do every step of ore processing in one machine, making it much faster, more scalable, and more performant than previous ore processing setups. The IOF should be the only ore processor in lategame bases."

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "Central Line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores or rare earths), Priority -1 for type filter routes (the default paths taken if nothing overrides them), and Priority -2 for output routes going to the final output chest.

- candidate `chunk-d3c0bb92e25671559f4130abe90a4322` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=1463-1724 distance=0.198858 similarity=0.801142 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"] text="MV EnderIO Conduits - The \"Central Line\"\nThis shows the simplest version of a \"central line\" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.\nEnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a \" central conduit line \" which all ores go through, and connected \" modules \" route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit \" priority \" system, which allows us to make override routes.\nThe priority system for the \" central line \" design goes as follows:\nPriority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.\nPriority -1: Type filter routes. These are your \"default\" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.\nPriority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.\nThe simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.\nSo you start adding \" modules \" to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module."

Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. - candidate `chunk-06d40bd7fed30e57f17a1a25576898d6` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2584-2984 distance=0.317030 similarity=0.682970 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="EV Applied Energistics 2\nApplied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:\n- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)\n- Maceration Stack (MS)\n- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium\n- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices,"

By replacing the conventional input bus with an Advanced Stocking Input Bus with auto-pull enabled, there's no need to store directly into an Input Bus, so the throughput is not limited by filling up said input bus. Advanced Stocking Input Buses can also be used to run recipe checks whenever their contents change, avoiding downtime due to recipe switches. This improvement is effectively necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike"
- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.343650 similarity=0.656350 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-c9c1517071de4cd1d65e85ed12a394c8` doc=doc-d38e0fb2c49edead8e172a0081f57d61 words=1241-1323 distance=0.344938 similarity=0.655062 sections=[Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing] text="Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing\nAs you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. - candidate `chunk-c8e59522b3ff87a5d0822136802a4e00` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=1513-1608 distance=0.347877 similarity=0.652123 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Integrated Ore Factory] text="Integrated Ore Factory\nThe Integrated Ore Factory is a large-scale ore processing multiblock that is unlocked with UEV circuits. It is able to process thousands of ores per second, and can do every step of ore processing in one machine, making it much faster, more scalable, and more performant than previous ore processing setups. Even with these benefits, it can often struggle to keep up with high-tier Space Elevator mining modules, requiring parallelization, overclocking with 2, 8, or even 32 energy hatches, or both. The IOF should be the only ore processor in lategame bases."
- candidate `chunk-899f089c10d9b05623dd29d55ffafa96` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2904-3304 distance=0.352702 similarity=0.647298 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. - context `chunk-d3c0bb92e25671559f4130abe90a4322` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=1463-1724 text="MV EnderIO Conduits - The \"Central Line\"\nThis shows the simplest version of a \"central line\" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.\nEnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a \" central conduit line \" which all ores go through, and connected \" modules \" route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit \" priority \" system, which allows us to make override routes.\nThe priority system for the \" central line \" design goes as follows:\nPriority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.\nPriority -1: Type filter routes. These are your \"default\" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.\nPriority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.\nThe simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.\nSo you start adding \" modules \" to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module."

Duration: 1910 ms
Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: GregTech New Horizons MV EnderIO central ore-processing line override default output priorities

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "central line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores or rare earths), Priority -1 for type filter routes (the default paths taken if nothing overrides them), and Priority -2 for output routes going to the final output chest.

- candidate `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 distance=0.329002 similarity=0.670998 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible] text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."

Auto-output buttons circled in yellow.\nLV Electric machines have some new features that were not available with Steam-age machinery. For example, the steam exhaust is replaced with an automatic output. This output's facing can be changed with a wrench similar to how the exhaust was configured on Steam machines. - candidate `chunk-de6bbc8fe923385317fcd50ba0bd904d` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=933-1239 distance=0.343187 similarity=0.656813 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > LV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters] text="LV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters\nAutomated ore processing is possible as early as LV because of the introduction of GregTech's Item Pipes and Filter blocks. The item pipes are extremely limited compared to future tiers' logistics solutions, but they have some key properties that make them usable for automation, while having major caveats:\n- The flow of items within a network of pipes can be in any direction.\n- Items put into a pipe network are pushed into the \"closest\" inventory that accepts them.\n- Distance is measured by routing value, where higher routing value means higher distance.\n- The distances of inventories can be coarsely manipulated using restricted item pipes which have extremely high routing values.\nCombining this with GregTech's Item Filter, Recipe Filter, and/or Type Filter blocks, which are capable of selectively accepting and automatically outputting items, enables a functional framework for ore processing. This system should ideally be hooked up to the steam multiblocks for maceration , washing , and centrifuging , as the LV singleblock counterparts have much worse throughput.\nOne way this system can be implemented with a centralized pipe network that connects to all machine input and outputs, as well as an input and output chest. Each machine input needs a Recipe Filter or Type Filter block in front of it, so that the only inputs going into each machine are inputs that the machine can handle. Another way to do it is to have multiple Type Filters that output into a separate pipe subnetwork that then outputs into a machine. For example, a Steam Grinder can be hooked up to a Recipe Filter block set to Macerator so that it accepts any item that can be macerated, or it could be hooked up to Type Filter blocks for specific stages, such as Raw, Crushed, Impure, or Purified."

Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "Central Line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores or rare earths), Priority -1 for type filter routes (the default paths taken if nothing overrides them), and Priority -2 for output routes going to the final output chest.

This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. Original query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?
Search query: What are the override/default/output priorities in an MV EnderIO central ore-processing line?

Status: answer

Answer:

In the MV EnderIO "central line" ore-processing design, the priority system is: Priority 0 for override routes (for example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.); Priority -1 for type filter routes, which are the default paths taken if nothing overrides them; and Priority -2 for output routes, which go to the final output chest.

At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:\n- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)\n- Maceration Stack (MS)\n- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium\n- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices,"

## baseline-rag / q04

Question: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Corpus sufficient: true

Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?

Status: answer

Answer:

When the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items may accidentally be routed to the normal macerators instead, which the source describes as bad. The design mentions that there are no easy fixes besides adding bigger buffers.

Status: answer

Answer:

In the EnderIO Conduits "Central Line" design, the main weakness is that the logic can break down if buffer chests fill; the system is not "truly" solvable because a large enough input can still break it. The design mentions adding more chests as a mitigation, though this never fully solves the problem.

Ideally you only want to change stuff in the current step you're dealing with (eg thermal centrifuging), not the whole line.\nUnbreakable\nNo matter what weird combination of ores or even non-ores you feed in, your system shouldn't break. At the same time, if your system experiences a power-outage, you should be able to restart your machines without catastrophic loss of rare materials.\nHigh Throughput\nYour choice of logistics system should not be a bottleneck for speed. For example, PRT (described in Pre-AE2 Autocrafting ) has very low pipe speed (beyond not being TPS friendly at scale), so it would not be appropriate for a late game ore processing system.\nLag Friendly\nYour choice of logistics system should not bring the server to its knees. This matters especially for late game players.\nMinimal Human Intervention\nYou want to be able to throw everything into an input chest, and receive finished clean dusts and/or ingots in your output with zero intervention. You should only touch your ore processing system for upgrades or debugging issues.\nOverview of Designs\nOre Processing Design | Tech Tier | Flexible | Expandable | Unbreakable | High Throughput | Low Lag | Minimal Intervention\nOre Processing Design: Limited Flexibility GT Pipes | Tech Tier: LV | Flexible: D | Expandable: F | Unbreakable: C | High Throughput: F | Low Lag: F | Minimal Intervention: C\nOre Processing Design: EnderIO Conduits - The \"Central Line\" | Tech Tier: MV | Flexible: S | Expandable: S | Unbreakable: A | High Throughput: B | Low Lag: A | Minimal Intervention: S\nOre Processing Design: Applied Energistics 2 | Tech Tier: EV | Flexible: SS | Expandable: SS | Unbreakable: S | High Throughput: Setup Dependent | Low Lag: S | Minimal Intervention: S\nOre Processing Design: Ore Processing Multi | Tech Tier: ZPM | Flexible: ? | Expandable: ? | Unbreakable: ? | High Throughput: S | Low Lag: ? | Minimal Intervention: ?"

This programming can get a bit tedious, so I recommend making a conduit probe whenever you can - this lets you copy conduit settings.\nA medium sized EIO ore processing system. The system can be further expanded by increasing the length of the central line (horizontally, vertically - however you want). Item filters are labelled with green spray paint. Electrolyzer module has recipe filters pointed at chest buffers.\nFinally, I add a \"transfer chest.\" This is just so that my macerator round robin logic doesn't accidentally get sent to the rest of the central line.\nThe Rest of the Line\nEvery module you add will look almost exactly like the macerator module. The only things you will swap out will be different filters and machines in place of the macerators.\nFor specific item overrides (eg. I want crushed bauxite specifically to go to thermal centrifuging), remember to use priority 0, as this will override items going to the normal macerator route we defined above.\nOn the right you can see an example of a fully fledged EIO ore processing line.\nHow Desirable is the System?\n- Flexible: S Rank. It is very easy to add new modules, and they can be added in any configuration (before or after existing modules) without breaking things. Filters are very explicit and can be examined visually with NEI-like images. Because of the priority system you are able to always add a new, higher priority exception.\n- Expandable: S Rank. All you need for a machine integration is a space for item I/O, and EIO lets you do input and output from the same side. If you need fluids later, like for rare earths, you can bundle an ender fluid conduit inside the item conduit.\n- Unbreakable: A Rank. While this system by default is very robust to random items thrown in, like backpacks and tinker tools (these will automatically go to the output chest since they have no routes), the ability for logic to break down if buffer chests fill is a major weakness. While you can always add more chests, it is never able to be \"truly\" solved - a large enough input can still break your system.\n- High Throughput: B Rank. Item conduits are by default quite slow (4 items every 0.8 seconds or so). You can upgrade them up to 64 per 0.8 seconds, but this is still much"
- candidate `chunk-abca98025457ab8409522aaf2857759d` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=1280-1680 distance=0.340697 similarity=0.659303 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Resource Shortages Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Waterline Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Circuits Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Other Multiblocks] text="rare earths directly is not yet possible, so alternative production methods must be explored, such as Rare Earth dehydration, bees, and blood magic meteors. Radon will also be needed in large amounts, so the radon loop should be built if one has not done so.\nWaterline\nThe Water Purification Plant, hub of the Waterline.\nLuV introduces the Waterline , a collection of multiblocks which produce increasingly pure water. The first two tiers of water, Filtered and Ozonated, speed up the cutting and engraving of wafers. The first grade of water is necessary for LuV progression as it is needed for the Netherite line. The second grade is optional at LuV, but it improves the yield and speed of the Nefarious Oil step, so it is recommended to invest in it. They will also be needed later on as the Waterline is even more relevant at higher tiers where high tier water is necessary for the production of chips.\nCircuits\nAfter the completion of the fusion reactor, it becomes possible to manufacture Crystal circuits. These circuits have a unique automation challenge due to how their \"CPU\" component is crafted; it requires a loop of autoclaving and forge hammering. In addition, the standard method of creating the CPUs requires molten europium. The Crystalprocessor Mainframe is the first UV circuit available.\nOther Multiblocks\n- Circuit Assembly Line : Creates a large amount of circuits faster and often with a reduced cost than a regular circuit assembler. Pre-fusion, a Circuit Assembly Line only provides a speed improvement and so is optional. Post-fusion they are necessary to create the new circuit line, Crystalprocessors, and all circuit lines after.\n- Cyclotron : This multiblock is shaped similar to a fusion reactor, and generates particles. A notable use for the cyclotron is to generate quantum anomalies to make Advanced Nitinol. Advanced Nitinol is needed for the Matter Fabrication CPU as well as other ZPM and higher multiblocks. Note that in 2.9, this multiblock has been depreciated and replaced by the Large Hadron Collider .\n- Industrial Autoclave : A multi-block autoclave, it is a massive upgrade to the single-block autoclave with reduced power consumption, as well as increased speed and parallels. It is highly recommended to create the large amount of crystal chips needed for crystal processors, as well as for processing Naquadah at far faster rates.\n- Industrial Arc Furnace : A multi-block arc furnace. Although"
- candidate `chunk-794a586a0993f64266bba06805c40308` doc=doc-04ef7ad9e1765bcf95cbd804c813863b words=3200-3600 distance=0.352528 similarity=0.647472 sections=[Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Nano Forge and Nano Resin Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Space Elevator Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Mega Apiary] text="a Nano Resin matching the element of the ore, producing a Filled [Element] Extracting Nano Resin. By electrolyzing the filled Nano Resin, the Chlorine and original Nano Resin are recovered, and the lanthanide is obtained in molten form. In addition, extracting the element via Nano Resin leaves Chlorinated Rare Earth Concentrate, which can be processed by any Nano Resin, regardless of what the original ore was. This can be done for two more steps, for Chlorinated Rare Earth Enriched Solution and Chlorinated Rare Earth Diluted Solution, and it's possible to use the same Nano Resin for multiple steps, making Nano Resin a very strong source of lanthanide elements. The available elements from Nano Resin are:\n- Cerium\n- Dysprosium\n- Erbium\n- Europium\n- Gadolinium\n- Holmium\n- Lanthanum\n- Lutetium\n- Neodymium\n- Praseodymium\n- Promethium\n- Samarium\n- Terbium\n- Thulium\n- Ytterbium\nSpace Elevator\nA Space Elevator.\nThe Space Elevator is a modular multiblock that can be made late in UV, after obtaining UHV circuits. Although it supports many different modules with various abilities, the only one obtainable in UV is the first tier of Space Mining Module, which can produce hundreds or thousands of ores per second using a non-consumed tiered mining drone, computation from a Quantum Computer , rods and drill tips of varying materials depending on the mining drone, and Helium, Bismuth, or Radon Plasma. It can also be configured to change the available ores and modify the chances of each ore being produced. Using the Space Elevator effectively requires robust ore processing, including any processing lines like the Platline or Naqline whose inputs come from ores, and sufficient automatic production of plasma and rods/drill tips of the relevant material. Although it is available in UV, it is expensive enough and available late enough in the tier that many players do not build it until UHV.\nThe Space Elevator can also be used to travel to any planet up to Tier 8, although it cannot be used to return, so it's necessary to bring a rocket or other means of teleportation to get back. This mechanic can be used to reach Tier 8 planets without the Tier 8 Rocket, and thereby gain earlier access to materials like Awakened Draconium and Infinity Catalyst. An upgrade to Tier 3 motors unlocks travel to Tier 9 planets in UIV.\nMega Apiary\nThe Mega Apiary is the endgame"
- candidate `chunk-5f5916d3f672b5b9e6d815efae63cd1d` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2240-2640 distance=0.353795 similarity=0.646205 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Rockets] text="Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .\nRockets\nUnlike most tiers, IV contains two different tiers of rockets and associated sets of planets that they unlock. The Tier 3 Rocket is available early in the tier, only being gated behind the IV Assembling Machine to make some of the parts. The Tier 4 Rocket, on the other hand, requires the Assembly Line, meaning it is unavailable until just before the start of LuV. In addition, both tiers require an upgraded rocket fuel, Dense Hydrazine, in order to use, which will require building a Chemical Plant for players who opted to use Cetane-Boosted Diesel for the first two tiers. Most planets from Tier 3 onwards also require an upgraded set of Thermal Padding, which needs PBI to make, and the Tier 4 planet Venus requires a full set of armor with the SpaceSuit property. For a full list of resources available on the Tier 3 and 4 planets, see the Planets page. The Tier 3 rocket also unlocks the ability to make a space station over Jupiter, although the Tier 4 rocket is required to make the Planetary Gas Siphon that makes such a space station"
- candidate `chunk-f87d9ed4d580fbe002c4f5e86e2c1fc0` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=1600-2000 distance=0.371450 similarity=0.628550 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line" Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line" > The Macerator Module] text="override routes.\nThe priority system for the \" central line \" design goes as follows:\nPriority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.\nPriority -1: Type filter routes. These are your \"default\" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.\nPriority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.\nThe simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.\nSo you start adding \" modules \" to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.\nThe Macerator Module\nFor every module, you must choose two things: the filters and the machines. For a macerator, we want to automatically send anything that fits these characteristics:\n- ore\n- crushed ore\n- crushed purified ore\n- crushed thermal centrifuged ore\nGT type filters are perfect for this, so let's add four of those and configure appropriately.\nNow I will add a buffer chest - this will hold items routed by EIO, but not yet processed by machines. If the buffer chest gets full, items will go to the next available route - in this case, the output chest with priority -2. This can lead to undesirable behavior with very large inputs - for example, if the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, it might accidentally get routed to the normal macerators instead (which is bad). Unfortunately, there are no easy fixes for this besides adding bigger buffers.\nNow I round robin extract from the buffer chest into my macerators. EIO lets you easily select this option by just hitting a toggle in the menu. For the connections to the macerators, I set input on green (from my buffer chest) and output on red. This programming can get a bit tedious, so I recommend making a conduit probe whenever you can - this lets you copy conduit settings.\nA medium sized EIO ore processing system. The system can be further expanded by increasing the length of the central line (horizontally, vertically - however you want). Item filters are labelled with green spray paint. Electrolyzer module has recipe filters pointed at chest buffers.\nFinally, I add a \"transfer chest.\" This is just so that"
- candidate `chunk-664c4a77b4e9c91ff1a950622ed70a1d` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2560-2960 distance=0.373959 similarity=0.626041 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > HV EnderIO Conduits + GT Type Filters Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="to provide build clarifications. Some recipes are outdated as the GTNH modpack has continued to evolve overtime.)\nSMRE Process Flow Diagram, Game Version 2.1.2.0\nEV Applied Energistics 2\nApplied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:\n- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)\n- Maceration Stack (MS)\n- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium\n- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least"
- candidate `chunk-c525faf801bcb0fc5beef1a125d48446` doc=doc-04ef7ad9e1765bcf95cbd804c813863b words=2560-2960 distance=0.374825 similarity=0.625175 sections=[Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > UU-Matter Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > UU-Matter > Elemental Duplicator Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Cheaper Crystal Circuits Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Quality of Life Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Quality of Life > Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatch Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Sidequests > Quality of Life > Laser Vacuum Mirror] text="the game, particularly for circuits, nanites, and the Space Elevator. In order to obtain it in large quantities, the new Matter Fabrication CPU should be used once the player has a Quantum Anomaly to use to craft it. It has a free EU discount compared to its singleblock equivalent, access to parallels in addition to the existing perfect overclock all Mass Fabricators have, and the ability to use multiple Energy Hatches to scale better. It can also be used to produce Scrap and UU-Amplifier, but this is generally not as effective as overclocking more or placing more Matter Fabrication CPUs.\nElemental Duplicator\nThe Elemental Duplicator is the multiblock version of the Replicator, which can synthesize pure elements directly from UU-Matter. It is unlocked in UV, although it also requires a Quantum Anomaly in its recipe. It is most useful for certain rare elements, such as Oganesson, that are difficult to produce in sufficient quantities with other recipes.\nCheaper Crystal Circuits\nThe UV Energy Hatch unlocks a cheaper recipe for Crystalprocessors in the Circuit Assembly Line using Crystal SoCs. These SoCs can be made by engraving Crystal Processing Units, but it is far faster to make them from Ce:LuAG instead. There are two machines that can be used for Ce:LuAG: the Vacuum Furnace , which requires a loop, and the Industrial Autoclave , which requires Oganesson for the recipes without a chance of failure. Crystal SoCs will also be required in UHV for that tier's circuits.\nSidequests\nQuality of Life\nAuto-Taping Maintenance Hatch\nThe final maintenance upgrade in the game is the Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatch, which infinitely prevents all maintenance issues on multiblocks, without requiring any input at all. It also continuously fixes maintenance issues on connected multiblocks, meaning that it is no longer necessary to conduct maintenance on a multiblock before turning it on. Wallsharing can be useful in order to reduce the number of Auto-Taping Maintenance Hatches required for large arrays of multiblocks, and since there's never a need to access them, they can be placed in inaccessible locations in order to save on useful shared hatch space.\nLaser Vacuum Mirror\nThe Laser Vacuum Mirror is an upgraded laser pipe that can be used to rotate lasers , although merging or splitting them still requires an Active Transformer . It requires UHV circuits as well as Chromatic Glass, the latter being made in a Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver with a"
- candidate `chunk-c63ead563fe713652b6ae7c65fd3f3c6` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2880-3280 distance=0.380318 similarity=0.619682 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.\n- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card"
- candidate `chunk-16d1ae576cd649fa3c6fee16783cff7a` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=960-1360 distance=0.381000 similarity=0.619000 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > GT Electric Machines Low Voltage (LV) > Explosions Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Conversion Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Conversion > IC2 EU Low Voltage (LV) > Energy Conversion > GT EU to Others] text="stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.\nSome machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . The Arc Furnace requires 3 amps to function and can accept up to 7 amps. Checking any recipe for the Arc Furnace will show Usage XX/t, voltage 32 EU/t and amperage X. The Electric Blast Furnace is even more demanding, taking four amps of LV minimum for its most basic recipes.\nExplosions\nMachines, wires and cables can overload, resulting in fires and explosions .\nRain will make your electric machines explode if the rain is on any adjacent blocks to the machine, so put your machinery under a proper roof. Uninsulated wires will also catch on fire from rain. Fire adjacent to machines will cause them to explode, potentially taking out more machines and causing significant Pollution . Water does not cause fires/explosions; it's perfectly safe to have water blocks adjacent to machines.\nGiving machines a higher voltage than they are rated for will make them explode. This won't become an issue before unlocking MV , but it's important enough to mention early and often. Excess Amperage on a cable is not an issue, as long as it doesn't exceed the cable's rating. Machines will only accept as many Amps as they need.\nEnergy Conversion\nIC2 EU\nTo transform IC2 energy into GT energy you simply need to place a GT transformer or power storage next to the IC2 power source. Keep in mind that IC2 generation is typically only 1 amp, therefore the Transformer should be in Step-Down mode. GT cables/wires can be used to connect IC2 machines, but pay attention to the EU output. Some devices such as the Stirling Generator output more than 32EU, and thus require at least x2 cable.\nGT EU to Others\nGT Cables can be attached to almost any machine that requires some kind of energy, allowing a single power network to run machines from most mods in the pack including IC2, EnderIO, Forestry, Railcraft, Galacticraft and more. Due to the idiosyncrasies of ENet, at least one GT machine (a machine hull will do the job nicely) has to be present for power to transfer on GT cables/wires. Placing"

Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?

Status: answer

Answer:

When the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items may accidentally be routed to the normal macerators instead, which the source describes as bad. The design mentions that there are no easy fixes besides adding bigger buffers.

This can lead to undesirable behavior with very large inputs - for example, if the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, it might accidentally get routed to the normal macerators instead (which is bad). The system can be further expanded by increasing the length of the central line (horizontally, vertically - however you want). Item filters are labelled with green spray paint. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

Duration: 1931 ms
Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?

Status: answer

Answer:

When the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items may accidentally be routed to the normal macerators instead, which the design describes as bad. The only mitigation mentioned is adding bigger buffers, since there are no easy fixes otherwise.

For a macerator, we want to automatically send anything that fits these characteristics:\n- ore\n- crushed ore\n- crushed purified ore\n- crushed thermal centrifuged ore\nGT type filters are perfect for this, so let's add four of those and configure appropriately.\nNow I will add a buffer chest - this will hold items routed by EIO, but not yet processed by machines. If the buffer chest gets full, items will go to the next available route - in this case, the output chest with priority -2. This can lead to undesirable behavior with very large inputs - for example, if the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, it might accidentally get routed to the normal macerators instead (which is bad). Unfortunately, there are no easy fixes for this besides adding bigger buffers.\nNow I round robin extract from the buffer chest into my macerators. EIO lets you easily select this option by just hitting a toggle in the menu. For the connections to the macerators, I set input on green (from my buffer chest) and output on red. This programming can get a bit tedious, so I recommend making a conduit probe whenever you can - this lets you copy conduit settings.\nA medium sized EIO ore processing system. The system can be further expanded by increasing the length of the central line (horizontally, vertically - however you want). Item filters are labelled with green spray paint. Electrolyzer module has recipe filters pointed at chest buffers.\nFinally, I add a \"transfer chest.\" This is just so that my macerator round robin logic doesn't accidentally get sent to the rest of the central line."

The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that the OreDict Card is capable of using a complex mix of requirements (limited to 120 characters) for the items being exported by the storage bus. Asterisks (*) serve as fuzzy placeholders, vertical bars (|) serve as OR conditionals, exclamation points (!) serve as NOT conditionals, and ampersands (&) serve as AND conditionals. The OreDict card does not support parenthesis.\nFor our purposes we will want the following definitions inside our ME Storage Buses, based on the machines they are facing. The brackets themselves are not required for the OreDict definitions.\n- To Macerators: crushedCentrifuged* | rawOre* & !rawOreOilsands & !rawOreBlackgraniteOilsands This means Ores OR Centrifuged Ores AND exclude Ore Oilsands, which cannot be macerated. This enables initial maceration of whole ores (from VMs) and maceration of centrifuged ores (from LTRs) to recover tertiary byproducts.\n- To OWPs: crushed* & !crushedPurified* & !crushedCentrifuged* &!crushedBastnasite & !crushedMonazite This means Crushed Ores that are NOT Purified and are NOT Centrifuged, as well as NOT Crushed Bastnasite and NOT Crushed Monazite This is needed because (crushed*) by itself also encompasses crushed, purified AND centrifuged ores due to the ways they are oredicted. The crushed Bastnasite and Monazite ores go into lanthanide processing.\n- To LTRs: crushedPurified* & !*Galena* & !*Sphalerite* This means Purified Ores that are NOT containing Galena AND are NOT containing Sphalerite in their names. This is needed as we want to export these 2 specific purified ores for indium processing later.\n- To Large Sifters: There are 2 strategies you can use. For either of them you need to increase the priority of the storage buses to be significantly higher than those on the LTRs as purified ores that can be sifted may be sent to the LTRs instead of the Large Sifters if you don't change the priority. You must also have enough/fast enough sifters to keep up with your your input or sift-able ores will overflow into the LTRs."

This is largely intended to penalize recipe switching or letting a recipe stop running, meaning that passive production of materials via fusion is the most attractive way to use Fusion Reactors. Fusion Reactors also have a very limited rate of power intake; it can take several minutes before a new recipe can run. - candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.378264 similarity=0.621736 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

- candidate `chunk-5ef457618522fb11f9bafd246c274848` doc=doc-a509849f031bb1dadb346a8565bf75e8 words=1438-1568 distance=0.347378 similarity=0.652622 sections=[Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) > Infrastructure > Power > Antimatter] text="Antimatter\nSee More: Semi-Stable Antimatter Stabilization Sequencer and Shielded Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix\nThe SSASS, the multiblock used to produce Antimatter\nAntimatter becomes much more powerful in UMV, thanks to the tier unlocking much better additives for the Semi-Stable Antimatter Stabilization Sequencer that allow for each one to produce over 100T EU/t when properly supplied. - candidate `chunk-0cb23b805ee0aaab05e8541b5eebd42b` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=1222-1325 distance=0.361761 similarity=0.638239 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Resource Shortages] text="Resource Shortages\nAside from the new materials, all of the Platline materials will be needed in massive amounts.
