- candidate `chunk-9525eeb54571877dbc8da9b496f467de` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=3224-3624 distance=0.371245 similarity=0.628755 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that the OreDict Card is capable of using a complex mix of requirements (limited to 120 characters) for the items being exported by the storage bus. Asterisks (*) serve as fuzzy placeholders, vertical bars (|) serve as OR conditionals, exclamation points (!) serve as NOT conditionals, and ampersands (&) serve as AND conditionals. The OreDict card does not support parenthesis.\nFor our purposes we will want the following definitions inside our ME Storage Buses, based on the machines they are facing. The brackets themselves are not required for the OreDict definitions.\n- To Macerators: crushedCentrifuged* | rawOre* & !rawOreOilsands & !rawOreBlackgraniteOilsands This means Ores OR Centrifuged Ores AND exclude Ore Oilsands, which cannot be macerated. This enables initial maceration of whole ores (from VMs) and maceration of centrifuged ores (from LTRs) to recover tertiary byproducts.\n- To OWPs: crushed* & !crushedPurified* & !crushedCentrifuged* &!crushedBastnasite & !crushedMonazite This means Crushed Ores that are NOT Purified and are NOT Centrifuged, as well as NOT Crushed Bastnasite and NOT Crushed Monazite This is needed because (crushed*) by itself also encompasses crushed, purified AND centrifuged ores due to the ways they are oredicted. The crushed Bastnasite and Monazite ores go into lanthanide processing.\n- To LTRs: crushedPurified* & !*Galena* & !*Sphalerite* This means Purified Ores that are NOT containing Galena AND are NOT containing Sphalerite in their names. This is needed as we want to export these 2 specific purified ores for indium processing later.\n- To Large Sifters: There are 2 strategies you can use. For either of them you need to increase the priority of the storage buses to be significantly higher than those on the LTRs as purified ores that can be sifted may be sent to the LTRs instead of the Large Sifters if you don't change the priority. You must also have enough/fast enough sifters to keep up with your your input or sift-able ores will overflow into the LTRs."
- candidate `chunk-f7f5b90c55529af7356929d02c537caf` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=463-863 distance=0.374332 similarity=0.625668 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Fusion Reactor] text="Fusion Reactor\nA Fusion Reactor.\nThe capstone of LuV is the construction of a Fusion Reactor. Once Europium is obtained, it becomes possible to craft ZPM components. The Fusion Reactor is expensive--a single Mk I. requires over 4,000 LuV superconductors. Despite this expense, additional fusion reactors become attractive immediately, both for other materials and potentially to generate power.\nFusion Reactors have a unique mechanic in that they require a large amount of EU to begin processing a single type of recipe, typically in the hundreds of millions of EU. This is largely intended to penalize recipe switching or letting a recipe stop running, meaning that passive production of materials via fusion is the most attractive way to use Fusion Reactors. Fusion Reactors also have a very limited rate of power intake; it can take several minutes before a new recipe can run. As a result, resources that are crafted on demand should use a large batch size.\nThe available recipes in the Mk1 fusion reactor, in rough order of importance, are as follows:\n- Europium is the most important recipe by far, since it's needed in large quantities for all ZPM components. It should be passively produced in a dedicated reactor due to its slow rate of production, taking nearly 6 minutes to produce for a single ZPM motor.\n- Helium Plasma is not strictly necessary in LuV, but will be required in ZPM to smelt Neutronium and in UV for the Waterline . In LuV, it can also be used for power in a singleblock plasma generator or Large Plasma Turbine , or in further fusion recipes for Sunnarium and Boron Plasma.\n- Duranium is not necessary yet either, but is an extremely powerful material for steam and gas turbine rotors. It is needed for Quantum Anomalies in the Cyclotron, and is used in ZPM to make Tritanium, which is needed for Void Miners and the Tier 6 Rocket.\n- Calcium Plasma, Boron Plasma, Neon Plasma, and Force Plasma are part of the \"plasma chain\" of fusion recipes, which extends through the first three tiers of fusion reactors, and produces plasmas with much better stats than simple Helium Plasma for power generation.\n- Sunnarium can be produced using Helium Plasma, providing an alternative to methods like bees , breeder reactors , or the Molecular Transformer .\n- Osmium can be fused from Tungsten, although it is extremely slow at"
- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.378264 similarity=0.621736 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-5004e6ed211b0cba547ca63f00be3953` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=1671-1786 distance=0.380375 similarity=0.619625 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Void Miners > Toxic Everglades] text="Toxic Everglades\nThe Toxic Everglades can be visited by making a portal out of Containment Frames and lighting it with an Alkalus Disk, which requires a ZPM Alloy Blast Smelter to make. On versions prior to 2.9 the dimension has a unique method of ore generation that was different from vanilla and GT. Notably, the Toxic Everglades features a large amount of GT++ ores, many of which produce rare earths as well as on-tier materials such as Europium when processed. By placing a Void Miner, all of these rare materials can be harvested easily."
- context `chunk-a5655d3941392cbbd7037763dac5c025` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=1724-2016 text="The Macerator Module\nFor every module, you must choose two things: the filters and the machines. For a macerator, we want to automatically send anything that fits these characteristics:\n- ore\n- crushed ore\n- crushed purified ore\n- crushed thermal centrifuged ore\nGT type filters are perfect for this, so let's add four of those and configure appropriately.\nNow I will add a buffer chest - this will hold items routed by EIO, but not yet processed by machines. If the buffer chest gets full, items will go to the next available route - in this case, the output chest with priority -2. This can lead to undesirable behavior with very large inputs - for example, if the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, it might accidentally get routed to the normal macerators instead (which is bad). Unfortunately, there are no easy fixes for this besides adding bigger buffers.\nNow I round robin extract from the buffer chest into my macerators. EIO lets you easily select this option by just hitting a toggle in the menu. For the connections to the macerators, I set input on green (from my buffer chest) and output on red. This programming can get a bit tedious, so I recommend making a conduit probe whenever you can - this lets you copy conduit settings.\nA medium sized EIO ore processing system. The system can be further expanded by increasing the length of the central line (horizontally, vertically - however you want). Item filters are labelled with green spray paint. Electrolyzer module has recipe filters pointed at chest buffers.\nFinally, I add a \"transfer chest.\" This is just so that my macerator round robin logic doesn't accidentally get sent to the rest of the central line."
- context `chunk-a61e46971fad35640888a9436665f7b2` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2016-2101 text="The Rest of the Line\nEvery module you add will look almost exactly like the macerator module. ## filtered-rewritten / q04

Question: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- When the Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, items can flow to the next available route and may be misrouted to an ordinary macerator.
- The design mentions using bigger buffers as mitigation, but presents no easy or guaranteed fix; overflow risk remains.
- expected source doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b/section-5a273eae1560c84c35279dea3938e36e

Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?

Status: answer

Answer:

When the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items may accidentally be routed to the normal macerators instead, which the design describes as bad. The only mitigation mentioned is adding bigger buffers, since there are no easy fixes otherwise.

Radon will also be needed in large amounts, so the radon loop should be built if one has not done so."
- candidate `chunk-9525eeb54571877dbc8da9b496f467de` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=3224-3624 distance=0.371245 similarity=0.628755 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that the OreDict Card is capable of using a complex mix of requirements (limited to 120 characters) for the items being exported by the storage bus. Asterisks (*) serve as fuzzy placeholders, vertical bars (|) serve as OR conditionals, exclamation points (!) serve as NOT conditionals, and ampersands (&) serve as AND conditionals. The OreDict card does not support parenthesis.\nFor our purposes we will want the following definitions inside our ME Storage Buses, based on the machines they are facing. The brackets themselves are not required for the OreDict definitions.\n- To Macerators: crushedCentrifuged* | rawOre* & !rawOreOilsands & !rawOreBlackgraniteOilsands This means Ores OR Centrifuged Ores AND exclude Ore Oilsands, which cannot be macerated. This enables initial maceration of whole ores (from VMs) and maceration of centrifuged ores (from LTRs) to recover tertiary byproducts.\n- To OWPs: crushed* & !crushedPurified* & !crushedCentrifuged* &!crushedBastnasite & !crushedMonazite This means Crushed Ores that are NOT Purified and are NOT Centrifuged, as well as NOT Crushed Bastnasite and NOT Crushed Monazite This is needed because (crushed*) by itself also encompasses crushed, purified AND centrifuged ores due to the ways they are oredicted. The crushed Bastnasite and Monazite ores go into lanthanide processing.\n- To LTRs: crushedPurified* & !*Galena* & !*Sphalerite* This means Purified Ores that are NOT containing Galena AND are NOT containing Sphalerite in their names. This is needed as we want to export these 2 specific purified ores for indium processing later.\n- To Large Sifters: There are 2 strategies you can use. For either of them you need to increase the priority of the storage buses to be significantly higher than those on the LTRs as purified ores that can be sifted may be sent to the LTRs instead of the Large Sifters if you don't change the priority. You must also have enough/fast enough sifters to keep up with your your input or sift-able ores will overflow into the LTRs."
- candidate `chunk-f7f5b90c55529af7356929d02c537caf` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=463-863 distance=0.374332 similarity=0.625668 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Fusion Reactor] text="Fusion Reactor\nA Fusion Reactor.\nThe capstone of LuV is the construction of a Fusion Reactor. Once Europium is obtained, it becomes possible to craft ZPM components. The Fusion Reactor is expensive--a single Mk I. requires over 4,000 LuV superconductors. Despite this expense, additional fusion reactors become attractive immediately, both for other materials and potentially to generate power.\nFusion Reactors have a unique mechanic in that they require a large amount of EU to begin processing a single type of recipe, typically in the hundreds of millions of EU. This is largely intended to penalize recipe switching or letting a recipe stop running, meaning that passive production of materials via fusion is the most attractive way to use Fusion Reactors. Fusion Reactors also have a very limited rate of power intake; it can take several minutes before a new recipe can run. As a result, resources that are crafted on demand should use a large batch size.\nThe available recipes in the Mk1 fusion reactor, in rough order of importance, are as follows:\n- Europium is the most important recipe by far, since it's needed in large quantities for all ZPM components. It should be passively produced in a dedicated reactor due to its slow rate of production, taking nearly 6 minutes to produce for a single ZPM motor.\n- Helium Plasma is not strictly necessary in LuV, but will be required in ZPM to smelt Neutronium and in UV for the Waterline . In LuV, it can also be used for power in a singleblock plasma generator or Large Plasma Turbine , or in further fusion recipes for Sunnarium and Boron Plasma.\n- Duranium is not necessary yet either, but is an extremely powerful material for steam and gas turbine rotors. It is needed for Quantum Anomalies in the Cyclotron, and is used in ZPM to make Tritanium, which is needed for Void Miners and the Tier 6 Rocket.\n- Calcium Plasma, Boron Plasma, Neon Plasma, and Force Plasma are part of the \"plasma chain\" of fusion recipes, which extends through the first three tiers of fusion reactors, and produces plasmas with much better stats than simple Helium Plasma for power generation.\n- Sunnarium can be produced using Helium Plasma, providing an alternative to methods like bees , breeder reactors , or the Molecular Transformer .\n- Osmium can be fused from Tungsten, although it is extremely slow at"
- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.378264 similarity=0.621736 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-5004e6ed211b0cba547ca63f00be3953` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=1671-1786 distance=0.380375 similarity=0.619625 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Void Miners > Toxic Everglades] text="Toxic Everglades\nThe Toxic Everglades can be visited by making a portal out of Containment Frames and lighting it with an Alkalus Disk, which requires a ZPM Alloy Blast Smelter to make. - context `chunk-a5655d3941392cbbd7037763dac5c025` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=1724-2016 text="The Macerator Module\nFor every module, you must choose two things: the filters and the machines. For a macerator, we want to automatically send anything that fits these characteristics:\n- ore\n- crushed ore\n- crushed purified ore\n- crushed thermal centrifuged ore\nGT type filters are perfect for this, so let's add four of those and configure appropriately.\nNow I will add a buffer chest - this will hold items routed by EIO, but not yet processed by machines. If the buffer chest gets full, items will go to the next available route - in this case, the output chest with priority -2. This can lead to undesirable behavior with very large inputs - for example, if the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, it might accidentally get routed to the normal macerators instead (which is bad). Unfortunately, there are no easy fixes for this besides adding bigger buffers.\nNow I round robin extract from the buffer chest into my macerators. EIO lets you easily select this option by just hitting a toggle in the menu. For the connections to the macerators, I set input on green (from my buffer chest) and output on red. This programming can get a bit tedious, so I recommend making a conduit probe whenever you can - this lets you copy conduit settings.\nA medium sized EIO ore processing system. The system can be further expanded by increasing the length of the central line (horizontally, vertically - however you want). Item filters are labelled with green spray paint. Electrolyzer module has recipe filters pointed at chest buffers.\nFinally, I add a \"transfer chest.\" This is just so that my macerator round robin logic doesn't accidentally get sent to the rest of the central line."
- context `chunk-a61e46971fad35640888a9436665f7b2` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2016-2101 text="The Rest of the Line\nEvery module you add will look almost exactly like the macerator module. - context `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

Duration: 2028 ms
Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: GregTech New Horizons Rare Earth macerator buffer fills mitigation

Status: answer

Answer:

When the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items can accidentally get routed to the normal macerators instead, which the design describes as bad. The only mitigation mentioned is adding bigger buffers, since there are no easy fixes otherwise.

- candidate `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 distance=0.333467 similarity=0.666533 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible] text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- candidate `chunk-996a60daafc37f1bcf77455008b22c82` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=0-151 distance=0.349382 similarity=0.650618 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM)] text="Zero Point Voltage (ZPM) is the seventh electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. It also sees additional power generation with the availability of the Large Naquadah Reactor and MK2 Fusion Controller, and a new source of resources in the Void Miner . However, similar to LuV, material costs and processing requirements continue to rise and so infrastructure such as a Mega Electric Blast Furnace , Mega Vacuum Freezer , and Mega Chemical Reactor may be necessary. Circuits get a major improvement with the addition of Europium-doped wafers. The PCB Factory is also build-able at this stage, though its quest is UV. ZPM is generally considered to mark the transition from midgame to lategame."

- candidate `chunk-06d40bd7fed30e57f17a1a25576898d6` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2584-2984 distance=0.384143 similarity=0.615857 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="EV Applied Energistics 2\nApplied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:\n- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)\n- Maceration Stack (MS)\n- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium\n- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices,"

## rag-grounded / q04

Question: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- When the Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, items can flow to the next available route and may be misrouted to an ordinary macerator.
- The design mentions using bigger buffers as mitigation, but presents no easy or guaranteed fix; overflow risk remains.

Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?

Status: answer

Answer:

When the Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items may accidentally be routed to the normal macerators instead, which the source describes as bad. The design mentions that there are no easy fixes besides adding bigger buffers.

Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that the OreDict Card is capable of using a complex mix of requirements (limited to 120 characters) for the items being exported by the storage bus. Asterisks (*) serve as fuzzy placeholders, vertical bars (|) serve as OR conditionals, exclamation points (!) serve as NOT conditionals, and ampersands (&) serve as AND conditionals. The brackets themselves are not required for the OreDict definitions.\n- To Macerators: crushedCentrifuged* | rawOre* & !rawOreOilsands & !rawOreBlackgraniteOilsands This means Ores OR Centrifuged Ores AND exclude Ore Oilsands, which cannot be macerated. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

Original query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?
Search query: What happens when a Rare Earth macerator buffer fills, and what mitigation does this design mention?

Status: answer

Answer:

When a Rare Earth macerator buffer chest gets overfilled, items may accidentally be routed to the normal macerators instead, which the design describes as bad. The only mitigation mentioned is adding bigger buffers; the text states there are no easy fixes besides that.

Question: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- Route 3 is the basic route to choose when gallium is already automated and twice as much rutile is desired.
- Its sequence is Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge.
- The route gives 2x more rutile (and therefore 2x more titanium) than Route 2 in the stated circumstance.
- These are basic routes, not the best full bauxite-processing process; chemical bath and/or bauxite slurry may be used for best processing.

Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If gallium is already automated from essence berries, the basic bauxite route that gives twice as much rutile is the one that processes bauxite through the gallium extraction chain rather than the simpler aluminum-only route. In GT:NH, the relevant sequence is: Bauxite Ore → (via Sodium Hydroxide) Sodium Aluminate + Gallium Hydroxide → Titanium Dioxide (Rutile) as a byproduct, with the gallium-bearing step doubling rutile output compared to the direct bauxite-to-alumina route. Specifically, the sequence is: Bauxite + Sodium Hydroxide → Sodium Aluminate + Gallium Hydroxide; then Sodium Aluminate + Water → Aluminum Hydroxide + Sodium Hydroxide; and Gallium Hydroxide + Sulfuric Acid → Gallium + Titanium Dioxide (Rutile). The rutile yield is doubled because the gallium hydroxide byproduct is processed for titanium dioxide, whereas the basic route without gallium recovery yields only the smaller rutile amount from the aluminum hydroxide side.

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium) than the Rutile + Gallium Route 2. For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- candidate `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 distance=0.309292 similarity=0.690708 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV] text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"
- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.317078 similarity=0.682922 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-51b7bee135bce54aa14f3ef7316450a3` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=495-633 distance=0.343364 similarity=0.656636 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium] text="Americium\nAmericium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach."
- candidate `chunk-48821e45dbe567c3c4946b397bd05ac8` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1669-1884 distance=0.345280 similarity=0.654720 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Progression] text="Progression\nProgression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:\n• Gallium -\nThere is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.\n• Arsenic -\nCobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.\n• Aluminum -\nAluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the \"raw Aluminum\" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum."

## fixed-structural / q05

Question: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- Route 3 is the basic route to choose when gallium is already automated and twice as much rutile is desired.
- Its sequence is Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge.
- The route gives 2x more rutile (and therefore 2x more titanium) than Route 2 in the stated circumstance.
- These are basic routes, not the best full bauxite-processing process; chemical bath and/or bauxite slurry may be used for best processing.

Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium). Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct).

As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.\nExpandable\nDepending on what batch you are processing, you may find a major bottleneck in your current system, or you simply want to replace machines with multis. This means your system must be able to expand without causing catastrophic infrastructure redesigns. Ideally you only want to change"
- candidate `chunk-85acdab6f2d774215e499224b8a83ff3` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1280-1680 distance=0.307771 similarity=0.692229 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > Blast Off \O/ High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > Open Computers Crop Breeding High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > Chlorine Automation] text="Titanium and Chrome), Bauxite (for Ilmenite and a lot of Aluminium), and Neodymium (for EV+ motors, Fluorine, Phosphorus, and Rare Earth elements that you need later in the game).\nEnd Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!\nSide Objectives\nWhile there are many upgrades to single block machines and entirely new multi-blocks to craft, not all of them are absolutely necessary to craft in order to progress to EV. However, some of these do provide excellent quality of life changes.\nOpen Computers Crop Breeding\nSee the main page here . After finishing the cleanroom, you will have all of the infrastructure necessary to build the crop breeding robot, although you will need epoxid as well as some progression in Thaumcraft. Note that this is an expensive build, especially if you have zero prior progression in Open Computers! The complexity and cost of materials rivals that of the NASA Workbench. However, following the quest book as you gather the components will slightly reduce costs.\nWhen completed, the crop breeder robot is capable of breeding a variety of new crops, statting them up, and even duplicating them for you! The only inputs required after the initial setup are a large number of crop sticks and fuel for the generator.\nChlorine Automation\nYou will quickly find that HV is completely miserable to progress through without a steady source of"
- candidate `chunk-5f13f1f234236c943e13b70a08107620` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=640-1040 distance=0.332445 similarity=0.667555 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > Overview of Designs Ore Processing Concepts > Filter Options Ore Processing Concepts > Special Processes Ore Processing Concepts > LV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters] text="Expandable: S | Unbreakable: A | High Throughput: B | Low Lag: A | Minimal Intervention: S\nOre Processing Design: Applied Energistics 2 | Tech Tier: EV | Flexible: SS | Expandable: SS | Unbreakable: S | High Throughput: Setup Dependent | Low Lag: S | Minimal Intervention: S\nOre Processing Design: Ore Processing Multi | Tech Tier: ZPM | Flexible: ? | Expandable: ? | Unbreakable: ? | High Throughput: S | Low Lag: ? | Minimal Intervention: ?\nFilter Options\nplaceholder\nSpecial Processes\nSome ores may have unique methods that can be used to obtain alternative, rare, minerals, or can extract more minerals per input ore.\nOre | Outputs | Notes\nOre: Chalcopyrite | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: Dissolve purified ore in chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. You won't get copper from this.\nOre: Tetrahedrite | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: Dissolve purified ore in chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. You won't get copper from this.\nOre: Ilmenite | Outputs: Niobium, Tantalum | Notes: Chemical bath purified ilmenite to get slag, which can be centrifuged.\nOre: Galena + Sphalerite | Outputs: Indium | Notes: N/A\nOre: Bauxite | Outputs: Rutile | Notes: Make bauxite slurry. Probably more efficient than regular processing line.\nOre: Pitchblende | Outputs: Radium-226 Dust | Notes: Purified pitchblende can be sifted for radium dust. Don't lick it.\nOre: Uraninite | Outputs: Radium-226 Dust | Notes: Purified uraninite can be sifted for radium dust.\nOre: Nickel | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: If you have spare mercury, you can chemical bath crushed nickel for extra platinum. Produces purified nickel ore as well.\nLV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters\nAutomated ore processing is possible as early as LV because of the introduction of GregTech's Item Pipes and Filter blocks. The item pipes are extremely limited compared to future tiers' logistics solutions, but they have some key properties that make them usable for automation, while having major caveats:\n- The flow of items within a network of pipes can be in any direction.\n- Items put into a pipe network are pushed into the \"closest\" inventory that accepts them.\n- Distance is measured by routing value, where higher routing value means higher distance.\n- The distances of inventories can be"
- candidate `chunk-5f5916d3f672b5b9e6d815efae63cd1d` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2240-2640 distance=0.339518 similarity=0.660482 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Rockets] text="Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .\nRockets\nUnlike most tiers, IV contains two different tiers of rockets and associated sets of planets that they unlock. The Tier 3 Rocket is available early in the tier, only being gated behind the IV Assembling Machine to make some of the parts. The Tier 4 Rocket, on the other hand, requires the Assembly Line, meaning it is unavailable until just before the start of LuV. In addition, both tiers require an upgraded rocket fuel, Dense Hydrazine, in order to use, which will require building a Chemical Plant for players who opted to use Cetane-Boosted Diesel for the first two tiers. Most planets from Tier 3 onwards also require an upgraded set of Thermal Padding, which needs PBI to make, and the Tier 4 planet Venus requires a full set of armor with the SpaceSuit property. For a full list of resources available on the Tier 3 and 4 planets, see the Planets page. The Tier 3 rocket also unlocks the ability to make a space station over Jupiter, although the Tier 4 rocket is required to make the Planetary Gas Siphon that makes such a space station"

- candidate `chunk-664c4a77b4e9c91ff1a950622ed70a1d` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2560-2960 distance=0.343906 similarity=0.656094 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > HV EnderIO Conduits + GT Type Filters Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="to provide build clarifications. Some recipes are outdated as the GTNH modpack has continued to evolve overtime.)\nSMRE Process Flow Diagram, Game Version 2.1.2.0\nEV Applied Energistics 2\nApplied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:\n- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)\n- Maceration Stack (MS)\n- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.\n- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)\n- Large Sifter (LS).\n- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)\n- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)\nOther multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).\nFor a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.\n- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium\n- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.\n- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least"

- candidate `chunk-fa69f174d015a45ccf16dbfd3761a3f4` doc=doc-8bdfdac1b12c28b48cfd59b3c35795d1 words=320-720 distance=0.352347 similarity=0.647653 sections=[Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Progression > Infinity Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Progression > Bio Circuits Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Progression > Xenoxene and Radox] text="the Neutron Collector, an Avaritia block that, when combined with World Accelerators , can supply Cosmic Neutronium before the Space Elevator is able to mine it.\nInfinity is required in moderate quantities for various UHV tasks, but gets used in large quantities starting in UEV.\nBio Circuits\nBio circuits are the UHV circuit line, going from ZPM to UEV, and are required for many advanced machines in UHV and almost everything in UEV. Just like Wetware circuits, they rely heavily on the Bacterial Vat and use the Assembly Line for UHV and above circuits. The Bio Lab is again required to produce the cultures used in the Bacterial Vat recipes, although these cultures are much slower and have much lower rates than those used for Wetware, encouraging the player to parallelize across multiple Bio Labs to obtain them more quickly.\nSimilar to Raw Growth Catalyst Medium, there are three recipes for Raw Bio Catalyst Medium. Generally, the best one is the one that uses tiny piles of Infinity Catalyst Dust; it is cheaper on materials and faster than the Tritanium Dust recipe, but avoids the difficult-to-automate loop in the Biocells recipe. Bio Catalyst also requires Seaweed Extract, which is made using another Bacterial Vat recipe for Seaweed Broth, and requires Unknown Liquid pumped from Barnarda C. The culture for this recipe is initially made using Seaweed harvested from T Ceti E, which can be used to make more seaweed for more cultures if needed.\nSimilar to Wetware circuits, the many slow machines required to produce Bio circuits leads most players to only use them for UEV circuits, where they are required, and stick with lower tier circuits for everything from ZPM to UHV.\nXenoxene and Radox\nXenoxene is a new fluid that is produced in the Bacterial Vat using Oil, Osmium, and Antimony Trioxide, and is required for both the new Optical SMDs and for the final plastic in the game, Radox Polymer. Obtaining the cultures for Xenoxene is infamously difficult, requiring many different slow and low-chance recipes in sequence, and since multiple cultures are needed to run enough Bacterial Vats to obtain enough Xenoxene for lategame, many players opt to passive said cultures.\nRadox is made by combining Barnarda C Wood and Xenoxene in an Industrial Coke Oven , and processing the produced Raw Radox through the Dangote Distillus or Mega Distillation Tower and the Mega Oil Cracker ."
- candidate `chunk-6433703bbb09054c0123d1292eb65c31` doc=doc-d38e0fb2c49edead8e172a0081f57d61 words=1600-1741 distance=0.353890 similarity=0.646110 sections=[Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Energy crisis - part 2 Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > End of EV Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Side Quests] text="energy (~30EU/t if 1x3x3 IV capacitor). You only need normal borosilicate glass to use IV and EV capacitor.\nEnd of EV\nAfter a trip back to mars full of ores (and also loots), you should have enough tungsten to get ready for IV. Also, you can make EV superconductor. It's cheap enough in late-EV, with superior performance compared to other wires. You also have to get graphene. It needs tons of silicon due to the amount of wafer it requires to craft (32 for P-doped wafer, 8 for Nq-doped).\nGood luck with your journey to IV!\nSide Quests\n-Eliminate microcrafting and improve automation and QoL with AE2 .\n-Build advanced processing lines for Ilmenite and Bauxite.\n-Make a Multiblock Miner for higher ore output.\n-Make various GT++ Multiblock versions of singleblocks such as the Bending Machine, Centrifuge, Lathe and Maceration Stack."
- context `chunk-a18470513100e5d5bd3a3c8f718df284` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=0-400 text="GTNH is all about technology (mechanical or magical). But lets face it, you won't be getting anywhere by just slapping those wooden logs together. All the metals you need have to be ripped out of the ground and processed from their useless ores into a pure form (usually dusts) for further processing. And that's why you're here.\nHow To Do \"Good\" Ore Processing?\nBauxite ore processing page accessible in NEI, showcasing various processing routes and their outputs\nAlthough there are many implementations of doing ore processing, the desired features of a \"good\" solution remain the same. These desirable characteristics are:\n- Flexible\n- Expandable\n- Unbreakable\n- High Throughput\n- Lag Friendly\n- Minimal Human Intervention\nFlexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.\nExpandable\nDepending on what batch you are processing, you may find a major bottleneck in your current system, or you simply want to replace machines with multis. This means your system must be able to expand without causing catastrophic infrastructure redesigns. Ideally you only want to change"

Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium) than Route 2. Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct).

- candidate `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 distance=0.252912 similarity=0.747088 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible] text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- candidate `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 distance=0.309292 similarity=0.690708 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV] text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"
- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.317078 similarity=0.682922 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-51b7bee135bce54aa14f3ef7316450a3` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=495-633 distance=0.343364 similarity=0.656636 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium] text="Americium\nAmericium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach."
- candidate `chunk-48821e45dbe567c3c4946b397bd05ac8` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1669-1884 distance=0.345280 similarity=0.654720 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Progression] text="Progression\nProgression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:\n• Gallium -\nThere is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.\n• Arsenic -\nCobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.\n• Aluminum -\nAluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the \"raw Aluminum\" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum."

Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium) than Route 2. Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge, yielding Rutile plus Grossular as a byproduct if using normal wash.

- candidate `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 distance=0.252912 similarity=0.747088 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible] text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- candidate `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 distance=0.309292 similarity=0.690708 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV] text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"
- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.317078 similarity=0.682922 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-51b7bee135bce54aa14f3ef7316450a3` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=495-633 distance=0.343364 similarity=0.656636 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium] text="Americium\nAmericium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach."
- candidate `chunk-48821e45dbe567c3c4946b397bd05ac8` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1669-1884 distance=0.345280 similarity=0.654720 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Progression] text="Progression\nProgression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:\n• Gallium -\nThere is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.\n• Arsenic -\nCobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.\n• Aluminum -\nAluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the \"raw Aluminum\" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum."

Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium) than the Rutile + Gallium Route 2. Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct).

For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- candidate `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 distance=0.309292 similarity=0.690708 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV] text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine).
