Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"
- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.317078 similarity=0.682922 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-51b7bee135bce54aa14f3ef7316450a3` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=495-633 distance=0.343364 similarity=0.656636 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium] text="Americium\nAmericium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach."
- candidate `chunk-48821e45dbe567c3c4946b397bd05ac8` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1669-1884 distance=0.345280 similarity=0.654720 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Progression] text="Progression\nProgression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:\n• Gallium -\nThere is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.\n• Arsenic -\nCobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.\n• Aluminum -\nAluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the \"raw Aluminum\" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum."

For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- candidate `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 distance=0.309292 similarity=0.690708 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV] text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"
- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.317078 similarity=0.682922 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-51b7bee135bce54aa14f3ef7316450a3` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=495-633 distance=0.343364 similarity=0.656636 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium] text="Americium\nAmericium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach."
- candidate `chunk-48821e45dbe567c3c4946b397bd05ac8` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1669-1884 distance=0.345280 similarity=0.654720 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Progression] text="Progression\nProgression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:\n• Gallium -\nThere is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.\n• Arsenic -\nCobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.\n• Aluminum -\nAluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the \"raw Aluminum\" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum."

Duration: 2747 ms
Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: GT:NH basic bauxite route with gallium already automated from essence berries that gives twice as much rutile and its sequence

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium) than the Rutile + Gallium route. Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct).

The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-48ef13f5915ef08f42de9de271e7ff30` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=1786-1940 distance=0.316883 similarity=0.683117 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Neutronium] text="Neutronium\nNeutronium is a new material that is needed in very large quantities in UV and UHV for components and other machines, and it is extremely slow to smelt, taking over two minutes at UV even with the best possible noble gas, and closer to three or four with worse ones. Because of how slow it is and how much it is used, most players passive it, setting up either a Mega Electric Blast Furnace (MEBF) or a large Volcanus array dedicated to passively smelting Neutronium Ingots. The MEBF can be scaled more easily and is much simpler to set up, but due to the high voltage and heat requirements for the Neutronium recipe and the 120% speed bonus of the Volcanus, the latter is more efficient. It is also possible to smelt Neutronium entirely on demand, but doing so requires extremely robust smelting and freezing capacity, or it will be a massive bottleneck."
- candidate `chunk-888c73bd962261aecef167f2c65e26de` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=1940-2054 distance=0.317247 similarity=0.682753 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Noble Gases] text="Noble Gases\nBoth smelting (including Neutronium smelting) and Void Miners can be vastly improved by using a high-tier noble gas. Oganesson is not practically obtainable in ZPM, but the next steps down, Xenon and Krypton, are. There are two methods of obtaining these gases: their respective bees or the Planetary Gas Siphon (PGS). The PGS is best used for Xenon, which requires a Tier 6 Rocket; each PGS can collect 350 L/s of Xenon when fed with 2A of ZPM. Bees are much more efficient on power, but the Xenon Bee cannot be used yet because it requires the Mega Apiary , meaning Krypton is the best noble gas available from bees in ZPM."

- context `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- context `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"

Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might choose Route 3, which gives 2x more Rutile (and therefore 2x more Titanium) than Route 2. Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct).

Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-51b7bee135bce54aa14f3ef7316450a3` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=495-633 distance=0.343364 similarity=0.656636 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium] text="Americium\nAmericium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach."
- candidate `chunk-48821e45dbe567c3c4946b397bd05ac8` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1669-1884 distance=0.345280 similarity=0.654720 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Progression] text="Progression\nProgression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:\n• Gallium -\nThere is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.\n• Arsenic -\nCobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.\n• Aluminum -\nAluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the \"raw Aluminum\" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum."

- context `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- context `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"

Duration: 1312 ms
Original query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?
Search query: If gallium is already automated from essence berries, which basic bauxite route gives twice as much rutile, and what is its sequence?

Status: answer

Answer:

If you already have automated gallium from essence berries, you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium. Its sequence is: Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct).

- context `chunk-47d289c4d1a14c32f00981954a28a1d8` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=116-353 text="Flexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators."
- context `chunk-f9a7893bcc78ce6dce97919745883b55` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1309-1491 text="End Of HV\nAfter collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.\nSpending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!\nInfrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!"

Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

In GT:NH, chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite is part of the ore processing chain for copper ores. Purified chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) is typically processed via chemical bath or similar chemical routes to yield copper, iron, and sulfur-bearing byproducts; purified tetrahedrite ((Cu,Fe)12Sb4S13) yields copper, antimony, and sulfur-bearing byproducts. The exact outputs depend on the specific processing step and tier of machinery used. A key caveat is that these chemical processing routes often require specific acids or reagents (such as sulfuric acid or sodium persulfate) and may produce hazardous or unwanted byproducts that must be handled or voided, and the efficiency can vary with the purity of the input and the machine tier.

Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum. The caveat is that you dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline, and you won't get copper from this.

- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.332771 similarity=0.667229 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

- candidate `chunk-899f089c10d9b05623dd29d55ffafa96` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2904-3304 distance=0.338626 similarity=0.661374 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.\n- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum: dissolving the purified ore in a chemical reactor yields platinum concentrate, which can replace or supplement using platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. The caveat is that you won't get copper from this.

- candidate `chunk-1992375dc86cb71e8274a9467c2fbce9` doc=doc-d8847ae5c01144e82bc225fe54375054 words=1920-2320 distance=0.322215 similarity=0.677785 sections=[Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Neutronium Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Noble Gases Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > UU-Matter Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Sidequests Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Sidequests > Wetware Circuits Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Sidequests > Other Multiblocks] text="entirely on demand, but doing so requires extremely robust smelting and freezing capacity, or it will be a massive bottleneck.\nNoble Gases\nBoth smelting (including Neutronium smelting) and Void Miners can be vastly improved by using a high-tier noble gas. There are two methods of obtaining these gases: their respective bees or the Planetary Gas Siphon (PGS). The PGS is best used for Xenon, which requires a Tier 6 Rocket; each PGS can collect 350 L/s of Xenon when fed with 2A of ZPM. Bees are much more efficient on power, but the Xenon Bee cannot be used yet because it requires the Mega Apiary , meaning Krypton is the best noble gas available from bees in ZPM.\nUU-Matter\nUU-Matter begins to see significant use in UV as a crafting component, particularly for circuits, in addition to its existing use in replicating elements. Because of this fact and how slow UU-Matter is to make, it's recommended to set up a singleblock Mass Fabricator to produce UU-Matter passively in order to prepare for UV, although it is also possible to make the Matter Fabrication CPU in ZPM by overclocking some machines and obtaining a Quantum Anomaly.\nSidequests\nWetware Circuits\nWetwares are the next circuit line after Crystal Circuits, spanning from LuV to UHV. The first three of them can be made in ZPM, but the fourth requires UV in order to make the Research Station for the Assembly Line Data Stick; this is the start of a pattern that will continue until the endgame of only being able to make circuits one tier up, rather than two as has been the case since HV. It is possible to replace Crystals with Wetwares for LuV to UV, but this is not recommended, as Wetwares are much slower and much more expensive than their same-tier Crystal counterparts.\nOther Multiblocks\n- PCB Factory : The PCB Factory is a multiblock that can produce circuit boards much cheaper than the Large Chemical Reactor ; it is especially useful for the expensive Wetware boards. However, it is unable to run any overclocks or parallels at all until UHV, or UV with meteors, which makes it impractically slow to use in ZPM, although Wetwares are expensive enough to potentially justify it.\n- Large Scale Auto-Assembler v1.01 : This multiblock, also known"
- candidate `chunk-c63ead563fe713652b6ae7c65fd3f3c6` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2880-3280 distance=0.323699 similarity=0.676301 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .\n- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.\n- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card"
- candidate `chunk-abca98025457ab8409522aaf2857759d` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=1280-1680 distance=0.325348 similarity=0.674652 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Resource Shortages Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Waterline Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Circuits Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Infrastructure > Other Multiblocks] text="rare earths directly is not yet possible, so alternative production methods must be explored, such as Rare Earth dehydration, bees, and blood magic meteors. Radon will also be needed in large amounts, so the radon loop should be built if one has not done so.\nWaterline\nThe Water Purification Plant, hub of the Waterline.\nLuV introduces the Waterline , a collection of multiblocks which produce increasingly pure water. The first two tiers of water, Filtered and Ozonated, speed up the cutting and engraving of wafers. The first grade of water is necessary for LuV progression as it is needed for the Netherite line. The second grade is optional at LuV, but it improves the yield and speed of the Nefarious Oil step, so it is recommended to invest in it. They will also be needed later on as the Waterline is even more relevant at higher tiers where high tier water is necessary for the production of chips.\nCircuits\nAfter the completion of the fusion reactor, it becomes possible to manufacture Crystal circuits. These circuits have a unique automation challenge due to how their \"CPU\" component is crafted; it requires a loop of autoclaving and forge hammering. In addition, the standard method of creating the CPUs requires molten europium. The Crystalprocessor Mainframe is the first UV circuit available.\nOther Multiblocks\n- Circuit Assembly Line : Creates a large amount of circuits faster and often with a reduced cost than a regular circuit assembler. Pre-fusion, a Circuit Assembly Line only provides a speed improvement and so is optional. Post-fusion they are necessary to create the new circuit line, Crystalprocessors, and all circuit lines after.\n- Cyclotron : This multiblock is shaped similar to a fusion reactor, and generates particles. A notable use for the cyclotron is to generate quantum anomalies to make Advanced Nitinol. Advanced Nitinol is needed for the Matter Fabrication CPU as well as other ZPM and higher multiblocks. Note that in 2.9, this multiblock has been depreciated and replaced by the Large Hadron Collider .\n- Industrial Autoclave : A multi-block autoclave, it is a massive upgrade to the single-block autoclave with reduced power consumption, as well as increased speed and parallels. It is highly recommended to create the large amount of crystal chips needed for crystal processors, as well as for processing Naquadah at far faster rates.\n- Industrial Arc Furnace : A multi-block arc furnace. Although"
- candidate `chunk-7561c0d4953ab63c18e2ee8e8e7d17a7` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4160-4545 distance=0.333602 similarity=0.666398 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Input Buses can also be used to run recipe checks whenever their contents change, avoiding downtime due to recipe switches. This improvement is effectively necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-27be4ec2aa30f8622e62a1587478255f` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=3200-3600 distance=0.334318 similarity=0.665682 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that the OreDict Card is capable of using a complex mix of requirements (limited to 120 characters) for the items being exported by the storage bus. Asterisks (*) serve as fuzzy placeholders, vertical bars (|) serve as OR conditionals, exclamation points (!) serve as NOT conditionals, and ampersands (&) serve as AND conditionals. The OreDict card does not support parenthesis.\nFor our purposes we will want the following definitions inside our ME Storage Buses, based on the machines they are facing. The brackets themselves are not required for the OreDict definitions.\n- To Macerators: crushedCentrifuged* | rawOre* & !rawOreOilsands & !rawOreBlackgraniteOilsands This means Ores OR Centrifuged Ores AND exclude Ore Oilsands, which cannot be macerated. This enables initial maceration of whole ores (from VMs) and maceration of centrifuged ores (from LTRs) to recover tertiary byproducts.\n- To OWPs: crushed* & !crushedPurified* & !crushedCentrifuged* &!crushedBastnasite & !crushedMonazite This means Crushed Ores that are NOT Purified and are NOT Centrifuged, as well as NOT Crushed Bastnasite and NOT Crushed Monazite This is needed because (crushed*) by itself also encompasses crushed, purified AND centrifuged ores due to the ways they are oredicted. The crushed Bastnasite and Monazite ores go into lanthanide processing.\n- To LTRs: crushedPurified* & !*Galena* & !*Sphalerite* This means Purified Ores that are NOT containing Galena AND are NOT containing Sphalerite in their names. This is needed as we want to export these 2 specific purified ores for indium processing later.\n- To Large Sifters: There are 2 strategies you can use. For either of them you need to increase the priority of the storage buses to be significantly higher than those on the LTRs as purified ores that can be sifted may be sent to the LTRs instead of the Large Sifters if you don't change"
- candidate `chunk-5f5916d3f672b5b9e6d815efae63cd1d` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2240-2640 distance=0.336246 similarity=0.663754 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Rockets] text="Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .\nRockets\nUnlike most tiers, IV contains two different tiers of rockets and associated sets of planets that they unlock. The Tier 3 Rocket is available early in the tier, only being gated behind the IV Assembling Machine to make some of the parts. The Tier 4 Rocket, on the other hand, requires the Assembly Line, meaning it is unavailable until just before the start of LuV. In addition, both tiers require an upgraded rocket fuel, Dense Hydrazine, in order to use, which will require building a Chemical Plant for players who opted to use Cetane-Boosted Diesel for the first two tiers. Most planets from Tier 3 onwards also require an upgraded set of Thermal Padding, which needs PBI to make, and the Tier 4 planet Venus requires a full set of armor with the SpaceSuit property. For a full list of resources available on the Tier 3 and 4 planets, see the Planets page. The Tier 3 rocket also unlocks the ability to make a space station over Jupiter, although the Tier 4 rocket is required to make the Planetary Gas Siphon that makes such a space station"

Horus Dungeons spawn randomly on the surface.\nT9 Anubis\nOre Vein | Weight | Frequency | Small Ore | Per"
- candidate `chunk-08fca16e5ad94adea6176b80969825ce` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=1920-2136 distance=0.337021 similarity=0.662979 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > The End and pre-Moon Titanium] text="an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.\nRaw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.\nThe production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.\nThe diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts."
- candidate `chunk-a18470513100e5d5bd3a3c8f718df284` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=0-400 distance=0.338057 similarity=0.661943 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Expandable] text="GTNH is all about technology (mechanical or magical). But lets face it, you won't be getting anywhere by just slapping those wooden logs together. All the metals you need have to be ripped out of the ground and processed from their useless ores into a pure form (usually dusts) for further processing. And that's why you're here.\nHow To Do \"Good\" Ore Processing?\nBauxite ore processing page accessible in NEI, showcasing various processing routes and their outputs\nAlthough there are many implementations of doing ore processing, the desired features of a \"good\" solution remain the same. These desirable characteristics are:\n- Flexible\n- Expandable\n- Unbreakable\n- High Throughput\n- Lag Friendly\n- Minimal Human Intervention\nFlexible\nOres in GT: New Horizons have multiple \" routes \" you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the \"best\" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):\n- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)\n- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)\nWhile for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.\nEvery ore in the game will have a different \"optimal\" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.\nYou also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.\nExpandable\nDepending on what batch you are processing, you may find a major bottleneck in your current system, or you simply want to replace machines with multis. This means your system must be able to expand without causing catastrophic infrastructure redesigns. Ideally you only want to change"
- context `chunk-5f13f1f234236c943e13b70a08107620` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=640-1040 text="Expandable: S | Unbreakable: A | High Throughput: B | Low Lag: A | Minimal Intervention: S\nOre Processing Design: Applied Energistics 2 | Tech Tier: EV | Flexible: SS | Expandable: SS | Unbreakable: S | High Throughput: Setup Dependent | Low Lag: S | Minimal Intervention: S\nOre Processing Design: Ore Processing Multi | Tech Tier: ZPM | Flexible: ? | Expandable: ? | Unbreakable: ? | High Throughput: S | Low Lag: ? | Minimal Intervention: ?\nFilter Options\nplaceholder\nSpecial Processes\nSome ores may have unique methods that can be used to obtain alternative, rare, minerals, or can extract more minerals per input ore.\nOre | Outputs | Notes\nOre: Chalcopyrite | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: Dissolve purified ore in chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. You won't get copper from this.\nOre: Tetrahedrite | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: Dissolve purified ore in chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. You won't get copper from this.\nOre: Ilmenite | Outputs: Niobium, Tantalum | Notes: Chemical bath purified ilmenite to get slag, which can be centrifuged.\nOre: Galena + Sphalerite | Outputs: Indium | Notes: N/A\nOre: Bauxite | Outputs: Rutile | Notes: Make bauxite slurry. Probably more efficient than regular processing line.\nOre: Pitchblende | Outputs: Radium-226 Dust | Notes: Purified pitchblende can be sifted for radium dust. Don't lick it.\nOre: Uraninite | Outputs: Radium-226 Dust | Notes: Purified uraninite can be sifted for radium dust.\nOre: Nickel | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: If you have spare mercury, you can chemical bath crushed nickel for extra platinum. Produces purified nickel ore as well.\nLV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters\nAutomated ore processing is possible as early as LV because of the introduction of GregTech's Item Pipes and Filter blocks. The item pipes are extremely limited compared to future tiers' logistics solutions, but they have some key properties that make them usable for automation, while having major caveats:\n- The flow of items within a network of pipes can be in any direction.\n- Items put into a pipe network are pushed into the \"closest\" inventory that accepts them.\n- Distance is measured by routing value, where higher routing value means higher distance.\n- The distances of inventories can be"

Duration: 1694 ms
Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum. The caveat is that you dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline, and you won't get copper from this.

The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.332771 similarity=0.667229 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-c9be8e2d914b8716772e72eed1d32b83` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=412-812 distance=0.335750 similarity=0.664250 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > Mid-HV] text="Mid-HV\nWith a more powerful energy infrastructure setup and running Cleanroom, you can start working on EV circuits, perfect for creating the HV Circuit Assembler. From now on, your copper consumption will greatly increase due to the massive demand from plastic circuit boards.\nYou will also want to look at the new multiblocks such as the Large Chemical Reactor, Distillation Tower, Oil Cracker, and Vacuum Freezer.\nThe Large Chemical Reactor might not be absolutely mandatory yet, but has some huge benefits: it has perfect overclocks, meaning that speed will quadruple every tier with ZERO additional power cost, it allows you to stop using cells for liquids, and it gates many extremely useful recipes such as a two-step PTFE recipe (for more LCRs) and one-step sulfuric acid from sulfur. The Distillation Tower will be your most expensive multiblock (requiring about ~56 Stainless Steel ingots for every layer), but the added efficiency in both resource production and energy consumption will make it absolutely worth it in the long run.\nThe Vacuum Freezer is not absolutely necessary until whenever you need Nichrome coils, but is worth crafting sooner than later. It is much cheaper to craft than you might expect (hopefully you have at least 2 and a half stacks of aluminium laying around at this point?) and massively reduces time and energy consumption for whatever Hot Ingots you may have originally been cooling using the Chemical Bath.\nThe Multi Smelter looks similar to an EBF but requires half the coils. It has insanely good efficiency and parallels while also being pretty cheap at this point, so it is highly recommended to get. You will most likely only need to build one of this.\nLastly, there are some multiblocks not mentioned previously that are possible to craft now that you have a cleanroom up and running:\n- Oil Cracking Unit : Replaces the hydrogen and steam cracking recipes that were done in the Chemical Reactor in previous tiers. It provides power cost reduction and bonus outputs. This is absolutely worth it for anyone using Oil to produce chemicals such as Ethylene.\n- Large Sifter : The first unlockable ore processor. It provides a massive boost to speed in the form of raw time reduction as well as parallels. In addition, sifting is a mandatory step in"
- candidate `chunk-899f089c10d9b05623dd29d55ffafa96` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2904-3304 distance=0.338626 similarity=0.661374 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.\n- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that"

Grade 6 or above water is also required for the most advanced Beam Line masks."

## rag-filtered / q06

Question: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- Chemically dissolving purified chalcopyrite in a chemical reactor produces platinum concentrate.
- Chemically dissolving purified tetrahedrite in a chemical reactor produces platinum concentrate.
- Neither route produces copper; the platinum concentrate can replace or supplement platinum metallic powder dust in the platline.

Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum. The caveat is that you dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline, and you won't get copper from this.

- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.298335 similarity=0.701665 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.332771 similarity=0.667229 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-c9be8e2d914b8716772e72eed1d32b83` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=412-812 distance=0.335750 similarity=0.664250 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > Mid-HV] text="Mid-HV\nWith a more powerful energy infrastructure setup and running Cleanroom, you can start working on EV circuits, perfect for creating the HV Circuit Assembler. From now on, your copper consumption will greatly increase due to the massive demand from plastic circuit boards.\nYou will also want to look at the new multiblocks such as the Large Chemical Reactor, Distillation Tower, Oil Cracker, and Vacuum Freezer.\nThe Large Chemical Reactor might not be absolutely mandatory yet, but has some huge benefits: it has perfect overclocks, meaning that speed will quadruple every tier with ZERO additional power cost, it allows you to stop using cells for liquids, and it gates many extremely useful recipes such as a two-step PTFE recipe (for more LCRs) and one-step sulfuric acid from sulfur. The Distillation Tower will be your most expensive multiblock (requiring about ~56 Stainless Steel ingots for every layer), but the added efficiency in both resource production and energy consumption will make it absolutely worth it in the long run.\nThe Vacuum Freezer is not absolutely necessary until whenever you need Nichrome coils, but is worth crafting sooner than later. It is much cheaper to craft than you might expect (hopefully you have at least 2 and a half stacks of aluminium laying around at this point?) and massively reduces time and energy consumption for whatever Hot Ingots you may have originally been cooling using the Chemical Bath.\nThe Multi Smelter looks similar to an EBF but requires half the coils. It has insanely good efficiency and parallels while also being pretty cheap at this point, so it is highly recommended to get. You will most likely only need to build one of this.\nLastly, there are some multiblocks not mentioned previously that are possible to craft now that you have a cleanroom up and running:\n- Oil Cracking Unit : Replaces the hydrogen and steam cracking recipes that were done in the Chemical Reactor in previous tiers. It provides a massive boost to speed in the form of raw time reduction as well as parallels. In addition, sifting is a mandatory step in"
- candidate `chunk-899f089c10d9b05623dd29d55ffafa96` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2904-3304 distance=0.338626 similarity=0.661374 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.\n- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that"

The High Energy Laser Purification Unit and Grade 6 water are not required until UEV when Grade 7 water must be made, but since it is a significant improvement over Grade 5, and UHV will require large amounts of wafers, it's generally advisable to make it sooner than that. Grade 6 or above water is also required for the most advanced Beam Line masks."

Duration: 1564 ms
Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum. The caveat is that you dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline, and you won't get copper from this.
