Produces purified nickel ore as well."
- candidate `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 distance=0.298335 similarity=0.701665 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines] text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

- candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.332771 similarity=0.667229 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. - Neither route produces copper; the platinum concentrate can replace or supplement platinum metallic powder dust in the platline.

Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum. The caveat is that you dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline, and you won't get copper from this.

The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."

This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process output is Platinum. The caveat is that you dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline, and you won't get copper from this.

- candidate `chunk-cbb24a351f234cec6664e9144021bcdc` doc=doc-c9afb2e028c318ddc2f228663f5523fe words=160-288 distance=0.331362 similarity=0.668638 sections=[Extremely Ultimate Voltage (UEV) > Progression > Waterline] text="Waterline\nLike LuV , ZPM , and UV , UEV brings two new steps to the Waterline , one of which is required in the tier and one of which is not required until the next tier but increases yield of components for optical circuits. - candidate `chunk-b91cca541a48a644cc92102fc6a3381b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=4184-4545 distance=0.332771 similarity=0.667229 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.\nAn alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of \"*\", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.\nAnd like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:\n- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).\n- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.\n- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)\n- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.\nAuxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:\n- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others\n- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases\n- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)\n- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).\n- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.\n- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here."
- candidate `chunk-c9be8e2d914b8716772e72eed1d32b83` doc=doc-8666c624815c422fd88b0cdfb5cbfb2a words=412-812 distance=0.335750 similarity=0.664250 sections=[High Voltage (HV) > Progression > Mid-HV] text="Mid-HV\nWith a more powerful energy infrastructure setup and running Cleanroom, you can start working on EV circuits, perfect for creating the HV Circuit Assembler. The HV Circuit Assembler allows you to make IV circuits, which are necessary for the NASA Workbench. From now on, your copper consumption will greatly increase due to the massive demand from plastic circuit boards.\nYou will also want to look at the new multiblocks such as the Large Chemical Reactor, Distillation Tower, Oil Cracker, and Vacuum Freezer.\nThe Large Chemical Reactor might not be absolutely mandatory yet, but has some huge benefits: it has perfect overclocks, meaning that speed will quadruple every tier with ZERO additional power cost, it allows you to stop using cells for liquids, and it gates many extremely useful recipes such as a two-step PTFE recipe (for more LCRs) and one-step sulfuric acid from sulfur. The Distillation Tower will be your most expensive multiblock (requiring about ~56 Stainless Steel ingots for every layer), but the added efficiency in both resource production and energy consumption will make it absolutely worth it in the long run.\nThe Vacuum Freezer is not absolutely necessary until whenever you need Nichrome coils, but is worth crafting sooner than later. It is much cheaper to craft than you might expect (hopefully you have at least 2 and a half stacks of aluminium laying around at this point?) and massively reduces time and energy consumption for whatever Hot Ingots you may have originally been cooling using the Chemical Bath.\nThe Multi Smelter looks similar to an EBF but requires half the coils. It has insanely good efficiency and parallels while also being pretty cheap at this point, so it is highly recommended to get. You will most likely only need to build one of this.\nLastly, there are some multiblocks not mentioned previously that are possible to craft now that you have a cleanroom up and running:\n- Oil Cracking Unit : Replaces the hydrogen and steam cracking recipes that were done in the Chemical Reactor in previous tiers. It provides power cost reduction and bonus outputs. This is absolutely worth it for anyone using Oil to produce chemicals such as Ethylene.\n- Large Sifter : The first unlockable ore processor. It provides a massive boost to speed in the form of raw time reduction as well as parallels. In addition, sifting is a mandatory step in"
- candidate `chunk-899f089c10d9b05623dd29d55ffafa96` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=2904-3304 distance=0.338626 similarity=0.661374 sections=[Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2] text="Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.\nFor our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:\n- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.\n- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.\n- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.\n- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.\n- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).\n- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.\nNow, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:\n- Galena Ore. oreGalena\n- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena\n- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena\n- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena\n- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena\n- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena\n- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena\n- Galena Dust dustGalena\nME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!\nAnother thing to note is that"
- candidate `chunk-c21e295084a34df53c76527aa37b5b5a` doc=doc-04ef7ad9e1765bcf95cbd804c813863b words=1039-1168 distance=0.340836 similarity=0.659164 sections=[Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Progression > Waterline] text="Waterline\nLike ZPM, UV brings two new steps to the Waterline, one of which is required in the tier and one of which is not required except as an ingredient to the next grade of water. The Extreme Temperature Fluctuation Purification Unit and its associated Grade 5 water are needed to process Americium-Doped Wafers, which are needed for QPIC Wafers for the Mk3 Fusion Reactor. The High Energy Laser Purification Unit and Grade 6 water are not required until UEV when Grade 7 water must be made, but since it is a significant improvement over Grade 5, and UHV will require large amounts of wafers, it's generally advisable to make it sooner than that. Grade 6 or above water is also required for the most advanced Beam Line masks."
- context `chunk-8bcbd9efb61d54acb8a89a128c69e87b` doc=doc-10abece1affc7c7ad6fb4e0605bf710b words=723-933 text="Special Processes\nSome ores may have unique methods that can be used to obtain alternative, rare, minerals, or can extract more minerals per input ore.\nOre | Outputs | Notes\nOre: Chalcopyrite | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: Dissolve purified ore in chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. You won't get copper from this.\nOre: Tetrahedrite | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: Dissolve purified ore in chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. You won't get copper from this.\nOre: Ilmenite | Outputs: Niobium, Tantalum | Notes: Chemical bath purified ilmenite to get slag, which can be centrifuged.\nOre: Galena + Sphalerite | Outputs: Indium | Notes: N/A\nOre: Bauxite | Outputs: Rutile | Notes: Make bauxite slurry. Probably more efficient than regular processing line.\nOre: Pitchblende | Outputs: Radium-226 Dust | Notes: Purified pitchblende can be sifted for radium dust. Don't lick it.\nOre: Uraninite | Outputs: Radium-226 Dust | Notes: Purified uraninite can be sifted for radium dust.\nOre: Nickel | Outputs: Platinum | Notes: If you have spare mercury, you can chemical bath crushed nickel for extra platinum. Produces purified nickel ore as well."
- context `chunk-7204ffb05b8f1f010ede14e35607675b` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=2194-2452 text="Other chemical lines\nPolybenzimidazole\nAlthough the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.\nRare Earths\nThe rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank ."

Duration: 1282 ms
Original query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?
Search query: What outputs and caveat are listed for chemically processing purified chalcopyrite and tetrahedrite?

Status: answer

Answer:

For both purified chalcopyrite and purified tetrahedrite, the listed special process is to dissolve the purified ore in a chemical reactor to get platinum concentrate, replacing or supplementing the use of platinum metallic powder dust in the platline. The caveat for both is: "You won't get copper from this."

Question: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- Crafting an LV solar panel requires being two tiers higher, at HV.
- Solar panels are not normally a main power source because their crafting tier is two tiers above the panel tier; they are supplemental power, useful for continuous or remote operations.

Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

In GT:NH, the gap is that LV solar panels are not a practical primary LV power source: their output is very low and they only generate during daylight, so they cannot reliably carry an LV machine setup through nights, rain/thunder, or sustained high-draw processing. A single LV solar panel produces only a trickle of LV-tier EU/t compared with what even basic LV machines and cables expect, and scaling it to useful output requires many panels plus significant materials and space. Because GT:NH power is continuous and machines often run unattended or in bursts, solar is normally used as supplemental/auxiliary power—offsetting some fuel or steam consumption, charging batteries, or running low-duty loads—while the main LV power comes from more consistent sources such as steam, combustion, or other continuous generators.

Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

The evidence indicates a two-tier progression gap: creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so to make an LV panel you need to be HV. Because of this tier requirement, solars are never a main power source, though they can help regular power generation, especially for operations that need to run all the time or far from the main power source.

Panels are quite expensive to make up for not needing fuel, especially more so if you're making them without the previous solar panel.\nUsage: Solar panels can be placed as a cover on a GT machine, battery buffer, machine hull or even cable, or crafted into a standalone solar panel block. Cover-type solars need periodic cleaning by right-clicking with empty hand while having a bucket of water in your inventory (can be done by golems), or their output will decrease. Solar panel blocks lack this disadvantage, also you don't need to protect them from rain.\nThaumcraft offers an option to make compressed solar panels. These take 8 panels of the previous tier to produce 10 times more power, so even if recipes become exponentially more expensive there's a bit of advantage. These also have the added bonus of being very TPS efficient, which is very important late game.\nStarting from triple onwards, it will require infusion. Read the Infusion automation guide for help on automating these solars. The maximum tier is 8 (Octuple), and requires 16777216 1 volt solars. This spreadsheet lists all items needed to create an UV Solar Panel and an Octuple Compressed Solar. The sheet is outdated for the former, since it was made before solar factory was added."

## fixed-structural / q07

Question: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- Crafting an LV solar panel requires being two tiers higher, at HV.
- Solar panels are not normally a main power source because their crafting tier is two tiers above the panel tier; they are supplemental power, useful for continuous or remote operations.

Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

The gap is two voltage tiers: a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so an LV panel requires HV progression. Solar is normally supplemental because of that tier requirement, though it can help regular power generation, especially for always-running or remote operations.

With access to electricity comes new hazards and mechanics, but also far more variety of specialized machines that can process materials into new parts with greater efficiency.\nGoals\nSome of the primary milestones for this tier are as follows:\n- Batch craft Electronic Circuits\n- LV components - Motor, Piston, Pump, Robot Arm, Sensor, Emitter\n- LV Machines - Bending Machine (priority), Wiremill (priority), Lathe, Assembler, Electrolyzer, Chemical Reactor, Fluid Extractor, etc.\n- Acquire Lithium and Lead for Batteries\n- Pump Oil for Polyethylene and Light Fuel\n- Upgrade Power Generation\n- Build Good Circuits\n- Locate Mica (or make the more expensive Alumino Silicate Wool)\n- Construct an Electric Blast Furnace & maintenance tools to get Aluminum\nOptional Side Quests:\n- Increase Hearts by eating a variety of foods\n- Plan for a larger base to accommodate MV machines / multiblocks\n- Make multiple Backpacks (Forestry/ModdedNetwork)\n- Hang Glider , Piston Boots , Healing Axe (if not already acquired)\n- Visit the Twilight Forest\n- More storage with drawer/barrel upgrades, Diamond Chests\n- Sound Mufflers, Chandeliers\n- Tool & Armor Upgrades\n- Item Dislocator (or another Magnet )\nEU (Energy Units) Mechanics\nGregTech energy consists of Voltage and Amperage. A Low Voltage (LV) GT generator will output 32 volts (32V) in 1 amperage (1A/1 amp). Four generators on the same cable will output 32 volts in 4 amps combined. 32 volts in 4 amps is not the same thing as MV (Medium Voltage - 128 volts per amp). This can be compared to four cables containing 32 volts each, or one 4x Cable. The x rating of a cable (x1, x2, x4, etc.) denotes its maximum amperage. The general rule of thumb is your cables should have an equal Amp capacity to the number of generators/batteries attached. Battery Buffers output 1A per battery , while virtually every generator puts out 1A. Having a cable with enough Amperage capacity for all of them at once prevents fires and explosions .\nFor more advanced and complete information, see Electricity .\nEnergy Loss\nThe tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length"

Ruridit as well as rhodium-plated palladium are used in huge quantities for even the most basic components and machines. Yttrium, Samarium, Neodymium, and many other rare earths will be needed in large amounts as well. However, mining many of the rare earths directly is not yet possible, so alternative production methods must be explored, such as Rare Earth dehydration, bees, and blood magic meteors. - context `chunk-0aaaf67e35c0220f24b54c5f8c40fdf0` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=320-720 text="helpful for getting other things on this list (e.g getting Platinum is integral to AE2, and automated plastics means that you can do much more processing with virtually infinite LCRs and circuits)\nPower\nStorage and Distribution\nAlthough it is possible to create centralized power storage and distribution infrastructure in earlier tiers, IV is the tier where any player who hasn't done so already should create said centralized power infrastructure. This power spine consists of a cable, or multiple cables if additional capacity is needed, with a high maximum amperage and a voltage usually greater than the player's current voltage tier. Power is transformed up when leaving the LSC to minimize cable loss and take full advantage of the cable's capacity, and transformed down for usage close to the actual machines. In IV, typical power spine cables are 16x versions of most LuV cables, such as Vanadium-Gallium, HSS-G, or Niobium-Titanium, depending on which is the easiest for the player to produce in bulk.\nGeneration\nIn order to take full advantage of this power storage and distribution infrastructure, it is necessary for the player to also greatly expand their power generation, usually to hundreds of thousands of EU/t by the end of the tier. In order to accomplish this, IV unlocks a wealth of new power generation multiblocks, as well as processing multiblocks that greatly simplify the process of generating fuel, while also saving on power compared to their singleblock counterparts. Players using Benzene should upgrade to Nitrobenzene if they have not already, upgrade to better turbine materials such as HSS-S or HSS-E, and use new multiblocks like the Industrial Electrolyzer and Dangote Distillus . Duration: 1427 ms
Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

The gap is two tiers: creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so an LV panel requires HV progression. Because of this tier requirement, solars are never a main power source; they are a viable power source from MV up to UV and are normally supplemental, helping regular power generation especially for operations that must run constantly or far from the main power source.

Lastly, Vacuum Reactors gain a massive buff in \"The Core\". \"The Core\" is the final fuel rod upgrade for vacuum reactors; it is extremely dangerous due to its heat generation, but produces a massive amount of energy.\nIn addition, a new method of power generation becomes available: plasma. Plasma produced by a fusion reactor can generate power in two different ways: placed into an Extreme Heat Exchanger in order to produce supercritical steam, or placed into a Large Plasma Turbine which directly generates power. Both methods will transform the plasma into its liquid / gas state, which can be potentially useful. Building a compact fusion reactor for power generation is the strongest source of energy available in LuV, albeit by far the most expensive."

Although other approaches exist, the most common way to do so is to use a Lapotronic Supercapacitor (LSC) as the main battery, fed directly from power generation (to minimize cable loss), and then distribute power outwards from the LSC to the rest of the base using a \"power spine\". This power spine consists of a cable, or multiple cables if additional capacity is needed, with a high maximum amperage and a voltage usually greater than the player's current voltage tier. Power is transformed up when leaving the LSC to minimize cable loss and take full advantage of the cable's capacity, and transformed down for usage close to the actual machines. Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

The gap is two tiers: creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so to make an LV panel you need to be HV. That is why solars are normally supplemental rather than a main power source: they are a viable power source from MV up to UV, but are never a main power source due to the tier requirement, though they can help regular power gen, especially for operations that need to run constantly or far from the main power source.

Solars are a viable power source from MV up to UV, but are never a main power source due to the tier requirement, however they can nicely help your regular power gen, especially in operations that need to be running all the time or far away from your main power source.\nProduction: Solars up to ULV are crafted in the regular crafting grid, then in the Solar Factory multiblock. Panels are quite expensive to make up for not needing fuel, especially more so if you're making them without the previous solar panel.\nUsage: Solar panels can be placed as a cover on a GT machine, battery buffer, machine hull or even cable, or crafted into a standalone solar panel block. Cover-type solars need periodic cleaning by right-clicking with empty hand while having a bucket of water in your inventory (can be done by golems), or their output will decrease. Solar panel blocks lack this disadvantage, also you don't need to protect them from rain.\nThaumcraft offers an option to make compressed solar panels. These take 8 panels of the previous tier to produce 10 times more power, so even if recipes become exponentially more expensive there's a bit of advantage. Octuple compressed solar panels can produce 100,000,000 EU/t, which is almost 200 times more than a UV solar panel. Moreover, there are infused versions of compressed solars which produce even more power under certain conditions. For example, octuple aqua infused solar can produce up to 600,000,000 EU/t while in thunderstorm. These also have the added bonus of being very TPS efficient, which is very important late game.\nStarting from triple onwards, it will require infusion. Read the Infusion automation guide for help on automating these solars. The maximum tier is 8 (Octuple), and requires 16777216 1 volt solars. This spreadsheet lists all items needed to create an UV Solar Panel and an Octuple Compressed Solar. The sheet is outdated for the former, since it was made before solar factory was added."
- candidate `chunk-b33c0a67b59566f01a7953640ba68dd4` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=110-154 distance=0.286101 similarity=0.713899 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Progression] text="Progression\nLuV is a much smaller tier compared to IV in terms of different milestones. The capstone of this tier is the Mk I. Fusion Reactor; it enables crafting Europium, which in turn gates T5 rockets, europium-doped wafers, the Crystal circuit line, and more."
- candidate `chunk-517bbd1b26feff56dfdafe2f4c8c18fe` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=39-201 distance=0.308796 similarity=0.691204 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Goals] text="Goals\nSome of the primary milestones for this tier are as follows:\n- Batch craft Electronic Circuits\n- LV components - Motor, Piston, Pump, Robot Arm, Sensor, Emitter\n- LV Machines - Bending Machine (priority), Wiremill (priority), Lathe, Assembler, Electrolyzer, Chemical Reactor, Fluid Extractor, etc.\n- Acquire Lithium and Lead for Batteries\n- Pump Oil for Polyethylene and Light Fuel\n- Upgrade Power Generation\n- Build Good Circuits\n- Locate Mica (or make the more expensive Alumino Silicate Wool)\n- Construct an Electric Blast Furnace & maintenance tools to get Aluminum\nOptional Side Quests:\n- Increase Hearts by eating a variety of foods\n- Plan for a larger base to accommodate MV machines / multiblocks\n- Make multiple Backpacks (Forestry/ModdedNetwork)\n- Hang Glider , Piston Boots , Healing Axe (if not already acquired)\n- Visit the Twilight Forest\n- More storage with drawer/barrel upgrades, Diamond Chests\n- Sound Mufflers, Chandeliers\n- Tool & Armor Upgrades\n- Item Dislocator (or another Magnet )"
- candidate `chunk-35faa3dc54bb97cc3c2bc9f644db1de3` doc=doc-2dca4aebd2d58cec651996f808e3aec7 words=1396-1482 distance=0.313610 similarity=0.686390 sections=[Tier > Tier > Mods by Tier] text="LV.\n- ↑ Gendustry requires significant bee breeding advancements (plutonium, uranium, naquadah, etc.) to progress and is mostly gated to LuV+. It's scoop and grafter unlock at HV.\n- ↑ Post-Moon; Personal Dimension is a Quest Book reward only, cannot be crafted.\n- ↑ See Stone Age Thaumcraft . The intended start point for TC is early MV. The Infusion Altar can be constructed as soon as a 40 vis craft is possible, if an Eye of Ender is acquired via Villager trade or other means."
- candidate `chunk-64ac91fc27b4dab9433816ad4cfe166a` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1400-1592 distance=0.315667 similarity=0.684333 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Revisiting Steam > Steam Power Upgrades] text="Steam Power Upgrades\nUp until LV your most automated options for generating Steam involved either regularly resetting Solar Boilers or collecting wood manually to feed Coke Ovens, the LV Crop Manager and tree bonsais allow for easy and cheap automation of Wood, enabling fully automatic power. Look into powering it with a semifluid generator directly with creosote, its a bit more power efficient and saves on pipe distance in most builds. You can try and breed the bonsais for max stats but that won't be necessary, even one 11x11 layer of 1/1/1 bonsais will provide more than enough wood for a max size RC Boiler . Speaking of RC boilers, the tank recipe gets substantially cheaper in LV, with the screw requirement being dropped with the assembler; the casing required for the tanks can also be made cheaper by utilising the Bender and the Cutting Machine.\nAfter visiting the Twilight Forest, the player can utilise the lead found to make Potin fluid pipes, which offer substantially more throughput than Bronze pipes of the same size. You can utilise the Fluid Extractor and Solidifier to produce pipes substantially quicker than with the Bender."
- candidate `chunk-58af5ab594c15228e96789f381b7b80a` doc=doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2 words=2790-2903 distance=0.322879 similarity=0.677121 sections=[Power Generation > Magic Generators] text="Magic Generators\nSimilar to Solar Panels are the Magic Energy Absorbers , which can generate power from LV to EV passively using energized nodes or a dragon egg placed on top of it. It is fairly expensive compared to non-passive EV generators, but considerably cheaper than EV solars, so it can be a good solution for powering multiblock miners, farms, etc in the midgame.\nMagic Energy Converters consume various resources, and make up to one HV amp. They can power farms that produce those very resources, for example 4 Master Magic Energy Converters can supply 1 amp of EV power to an Extreme Entity Crusher that makes Forbidden Magic shards among other things."
- candidate `chunk-c4f515f28759c9259bd668bf7140e214` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=0-110 distance=0.323104 similarity=0.676896 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV)] text="Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) is the sixth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier is largely centered around building the infrastructure necessary to construct the first tier of Fusion Reactor , as well as the new items and machines gated by fusion. This is the first tier where the Assembly Line is used to craft on-tier components as well as highly advanced machines. In addition, the costs and crafting trees for machines are even larger than in previous tiers, making fully automated on-demand crafting with AE2 absolutely necessary. The massive demand for robust infrastructure continues for the rest of the game; arrays of Volcanus consuming on-tier voltage are highly suggested."
- candidate `chunk-d4045ef03267b364c037d91490581bc5` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=961-1221 distance=0.325620 similarity=0.674380 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Power > Generation] text="Generation\nLike the previous tier IV , power generation capacity should follow the trend of exponential increase in order to accommodate the increasing number of energy-intensive processes. Several new multiblocks are now possible to construct which keeps some older power generation methods viable:\n- XL Turbo Gas Turbine\n- Universal Chemical Fuel Engine\n- Whakawhiti Wera XL\n- XL Turbo HP Steam Turbine\nDespite the upgrade to the UCFE, power generation from oil processing begins to fall off after this tier. Nitrobenzene gains a massive buff from the XLGT largely due to scalability, since turbines no longer need to be manually replaced, and only one multi-amp / laser dynamo is needed for a multiblock that generates 16x the power of a single LGT. Like oil, this is the last tier where benzene gains a direct upgrade. Lastly, Vacuum Reactors gain a massive buff in \"The Core\". \"The Core\" is the final fuel rod upgrade for vacuum reactors; it is extremely dangerous due to its heat generation, but produces a massive amount of energy.\nIn addition, a new method of power generation becomes available: plasma. Plasma produced by a fusion reactor can generate power in two different ways: placed into an Extreme Heat Exchanger in order to produce supercritical steam, or placed into a Large Plasma Turbine which directly generates power. Both methods will transform the plasma into its liquid / gas state, which can be potentially useful. Building a compact fusion reactor for power generation is the strongest source of energy available in LuV, albeit by far the most expensive."
- candidate `chunk-60ef21b85a35f0ea2add28c516390d50` doc=doc-2e161bb7490c4c12a7e195acd1873420 words=1325-1377 distance=0.327108 similarity=0.672892 sections=[Insanely Ultimate Voltage (UIV) > Infrastructure > Power] text="Power\nUIV continues to scale power demands, causing Naquadah Fuel to begin to fall off and plasma to fall out of viability. However, unlike UEV, it also introduces two new methods of power generation: Dyson Swarms and Antimatter. It also adds the first Wireless Energy Hatches, which greatly simplify power distribution logistics."
- candidate `chunk-54b631d0e6f01da5dd9ca91eb9a202b1` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=353-531 distance=0.328603 similarity=0.671397 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Power > Storage and Distribution] text="Storage and Distribution\nAlthough it is possible to create centralized power storage and distribution infrastructure in earlier tiers, IV is the tier where any player who hasn't done so already should create said centralized power infrastructure. Although other approaches exist, the most common way to do so is to use a Lapotronic Supercapacitor (LSC) as the main battery, fed directly from power generation (to minimize cable loss), and then distribute power outwards from the LSC to the rest of the base using a \"power spine\". This power spine consists of a cable, or multiple cables if additional capacity is needed, with a high maximum amperage and a voltage usually greater than the player's current voltage tier. Power is transformed up when leaving the LSC to minimize cable loss and take full advantage of the cable's capacity, and transformed down for usage close to the actual machines. In IV, typical power spine cables are 16x versions of most LuV cables, such as Vanadium-Gallium, HSS-G, or Niobium-Titanium, depending on which is the easiest for the player to produce in bulk."

## filtered-rewritten / q07

Question: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Corpus sufficient: true
Expected facts:
- Crafting an LV solar panel requires being two tiers higher, at HV.
- Solar panels are not normally a main power source because their crafting tier is two tiers above the panel tier; they are supplemental power, useful for continuous or remote operations.
- expected source doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2/section-987313dd8dc4716d75ee58791ab35c82

Duration: 1787 ms
Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

The evidence indicates a two-tier crafting requirement: to make a solar panel of a given tier, you must be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so an LV panel requires HV. That creates a progression gap between when LV power is used and when LV solar panels can actually be crafted. Solar is normally supplemental because of that tier requirement; the wiki says solars are a viable power source from MV up to UV but are never a main power source due to the tier requirement, though they can help regular power generation, especially for operations that must run constantly or far from the main power source.

- candidate `chunk-54b631d0e6f01da5dd9ca91eb9a202b1` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=353-531 distance=0.328603 similarity=0.671397 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Power > Storage and Distribution] text="Storage and Distribution\nAlthough it is possible to create centralized power storage and distribution infrastructure in earlier tiers, IV is the tier where any player who hasn't done so already should create said centralized power infrastructure. Although other approaches exist, the most common way to do so is to use a Lapotronic Supercapacitor (LSC) as the main battery, fed directly from power generation (to minimize cable loss), and then distribute power outwards from the LSC to the rest of the base using a \"power spine\". This power spine consists of a cable, or multiple cables if additional capacity is needed, with a high maximum amperage and a voltage usually greater than the player's current voltage tier. Power is transformed up when leaving the LSC to minimize cable loss and take full advantage of the cable's capacity, and transformed down for usage close to the actual machines. In IV, typical power spine cables are 16x versions of most LuV cables, such as Vanadium-Gallium, HSS-G, or Niobium-Titanium, depending on which is the easiest for the player to produce in bulk."

Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: GregTech New Horizons LV solar panel crafting progression gap LV power use why solar supplemental

Status: answer

Answer:

The gap is a two-tier crafting requirement: a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so an LV panel requires HV to craft. That means LV solar panels cannot be made at LV, which is why solars are never a main power source and are normally supplemental—they are a viable power source from MV up to UV, but the tier requirement keeps them from being primary, though they can help regular power generation, especially for operations that must run constantly or far from the main power source.

- candidate `chunk-64ac91fc27b4dab9433816ad4cfe166a` doc=doc-626c925b618145e4e43655f7673b36b4 words=1400-1592 distance=0.315667 similarity=0.684333 sections=[Low Voltage (LV) > Revisiting Steam > Steam Power Upgrades] text="Steam Power Upgrades\nUp until LV your most automated options for generating Steam involved either regularly resetting Solar Boilers or collecting wood manually to feed Coke Ovens, the LV Crop Manager and tree bonsais allow for easy and cheap automation of Wood, enabling fully automatic power. Look into powering it with a semifluid generator directly with creosote, its a bit more power efficient and saves on pipe distance in most builds. You can try and breed the bonsais for max stats but that won't be necessary, even one 11x11 layer of 1/1/1 bonsais will provide more than enough wood for a max size RC Boiler . Speaking of RC boilers, the tank recipe gets substantially cheaper in LV, with the screw requirement being dropped with the assembler; the casing required for the tanks can also be made cheaper by utilising the Bender and the Cutting Machine.\nAfter visiting the Twilight Forest, the player can utilise the lead found to make Potin fluid pipes, which offer substantially more throughput than Bronze pipes of the same size. You can utilise the Fluid Extractor and Solidifier to produce pipes substantially quicker than with the Bender."
- candidate `chunk-58af5ab594c15228e96789f381b7b80a` doc=doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2 words=2790-2903 distance=0.322879 similarity=0.677121 sections=[Power Generation > Magic Generators] text="Magic Generators\nSimilar to Solar Panels are the Magic Energy Absorbers , which can generate power from LV to EV passively using energized nodes or a dragon egg placed on top of it. It is fairly expensive compared to non-passive EV generators, but considerably cheaper than EV solars, so it can be a good solution for powering multiblock miners, farms, etc in the midgame.\nMagic Energy Converters consume various resources, and make up to one HV amp. - candidate `chunk-c4f515f28759c9259bd668bf7140e214` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=0-110 distance=0.323104 similarity=0.676896 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV)] text="Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) is the sixth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier is largely centered around building the infrastructure necessary to construct the first tier of Fusion Reactor , as well as the new items and machines gated by fusion. This is the first tier where the Assembly Line is used to craft on-tier components as well as highly advanced machines. In addition, the costs and crafting trees for machines are even larger than in previous tiers, making fully automated on-demand crafting with AE2 absolutely necessary. The massive demand for robust infrastructure continues for the rest of the game; arrays of Volcanus consuming on-tier voltage are highly suggested."
- candidate `chunk-d4045ef03267b364c037d91490581bc5` doc=doc-a9f4f7813df646e0e5f0ab08ab29b50e words=961-1221 distance=0.325620 similarity=0.674380 sections=[Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) > Power > Generation] text="Generation\nLike the previous tier IV , power generation capacity should follow the trend of exponential increase in order to accommodate the increasing number of energy-intensive processes. Several new multiblocks are now possible to construct which keeps some older power generation methods viable:\n- XL Turbo Gas Turbine\n- Universal Chemical Fuel Engine\n- Whakawhiti Wera XL\n- XL Turbo HP Steam Turbine\nDespite the upgrade to the UCFE, power generation from oil processing begins to fall off after this tier. Nitrobenzene gains a massive buff from the XLGT largely due to scalability, since turbines no longer need to be manually replaced, and only one multi-amp / laser dynamo is needed for a multiblock that generates 16x the power of a single LGT. Like oil, this is the last tier where benzene gains a direct upgrade. Lastly, Vacuum Reactors gain a massive buff in \"The Core\". \"The Core\" is the final fuel rod upgrade for vacuum reactors; it is extremely dangerous due to its heat generation, but produces a massive amount of energy.\nIn addition, a new method of power generation becomes available: plasma. Plasma produced by a fusion reactor can generate power in two different ways: placed into an Extreme Heat Exchanger in order to produce supercritical steam, or placed into a Large Plasma Turbine which directly generates power. Both methods will transform the plasma into its liquid / gas state, which can be potentially useful. Building a compact fusion reactor for power generation is the strongest source of energy available in LuV, albeit by far the most expensive."
- candidate `chunk-60ef21b85a35f0ea2add28c516390d50` doc=doc-2e161bb7490c4c12a7e195acd1873420 words=1325-1377 distance=0.327108 similarity=0.672892 sections=[Insanely Ultimate Voltage (UIV) > Infrastructure > Power] text="Power\nUIV continues to scale power demands, causing Naquadah Fuel to begin to fall off and plasma to fall out of viability. However, unlike UEV, it also introduces two new methods of power generation: Dyson Swarms and Antimatter. It also adds the first Wireless Energy Hatches, which greatly simplify power distribution logistics."
- candidate `chunk-54b631d0e6f01da5dd9ca91eb9a202b1` doc=doc-0acf46d9067c834f0c19087002ed00b0 words=353-531 distance=0.328603 similarity=0.671397 sections=[Insane Voltage (IV) > Power > Storage and Distribution] text="Storage and Distribution\nAlthough it is possible to create centralized power storage and distribution infrastructure in earlier tiers, IV is the tier where any player who hasn't done so already should create said centralized power infrastructure. Although other approaches exist, the most common way to do so is to use a Lapotronic Supercapacitor (LSC) as the main battery, fed directly from power generation (to minimize cable loss), and then distribute power outwards from the LSC to the rest of the base using a \"power spine\". This power spine consists of a cable, or multiple cables if additional capacity is needed, with a high maximum amperage and a voltage usually greater than the player's current voltage tier. Power is transformed up when leaving the LSC to minimize cable loss and take full advantage of the cable's capacity, and transformed down for usage close to the actual machines. In IV, typical power spine cables are 16x versions of most LuV cables, such as Vanadium-Gallium, HSS-G, or Niobium-Titanium, depending on which is the easiest for the player to produce in bulk."
- context `chunk-ecf1c03449abec6843b9508086ea1f0d` doc=doc-709fa05c9dc5e6bdd1e4979266413ad2 words=2411-2790 text="Solar Panels\nSolar panels are available in tiers from 1 EU/t all the way up to UV (524288 EU/t). Creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel (i.e. to make a LV panel you need to be HV). Solars are a viable power source from MV up to UV, but are never a main power source due to the tier requirement, however they can nicely help your regular power gen, especially in operations that need to be running all the time or far away from your main power source.\nProduction: Solars up to ULV are crafted in the regular crafting grid, then in the Solar Factory multiblock. Panels are quite expensive to make up for not needing fuel, especially more so if you're making them without the previous solar panel.\nUsage: Solar panels can be placed as a cover on a GT machine, battery buffer, machine hull or even cable, or crafted into a standalone solar panel block. Cover-type solars need periodic cleaning by right-clicking with empty hand while having a bucket of water in your inventory (can be done by golems), or their output will decrease. Solar panel blocks lack this disadvantage, also you don't need to protect them from rain.\nThaumcraft offers an option to make compressed solar panels. These take 8 panels of the previous tier to produce 10 times more power, so even if recipes become exponentially more expensive there's a bit of advantage. Octuple compressed solar panels can produce 100,000,000 EU/t, which is almost 200 times more than a UV solar panel. Moreover, there are infused versions of compressed solars which produce even more power under certain conditions. For example, octuple aqua infused solar can produce up to 600,000,000 EU/t while in thunderstorm. These also have the added bonus of being very TPS efficient, which is very important late game.\nStarting from triple onwards, it will require infusion. Read the Infusion automation guide for help on automating these solars. The maximum tier is 8 (Octuple), and requires 16777216 1 volt solars. This spreadsheet lists all items needed to create an UV Solar Panel and an Octuple Compressed Solar. The sheet is outdated for the former, since it was made before solar factory was added."

Duration: 1391 ms
Original query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?
Search query: What progression gap separates LV solar-panel crafting from LV power use, and why is solar normally supplemental?

Status: answer

Answer:

The evidence describes a tier gap: creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel, so to make an LV panel you need to be HV. That means LV solar-panel crafting is gated behind HV progression, while LV power use is available at the LV tier. Solar is normally supplemental because, due to that tier requirement, solars are never a main power source; they are a viable power source from MV up to UV and can help regular power generation, especially for operations that need to run all the time or far away from the main power source.
